ARCHITECTURE.html.title: ProvostXMemory — ARCHITECTURE | ProvostXMemory API
ARCHITECTURE.html.summary: ProvostXMemory — ARCHITECTURE License: MIT. Status: complete, audited (2026-10-13). Target: .NET 8. Summary: atomic, encapsulated .NET 8 memory/RAG library; hosts see only IMemoryService + typed options and inject their own embedder/grader/rewriter/telemetry; backends pluggable by config over an OWN C# vector engine (zero third-party vector dependencies); memory isolated per scope (platform/session/tenant/purpose/custom) by construction. Principles Strict OOP: interfaces first, constructor injection, no statics (pure-factory exceptions), one type per file Library knows NOTHING about its hosts; hosts know nothing about the internals No env vars in product code — config via typed options injected by the host All file I/O transactional (temp + atomic swap) at the storage layer Every public operation is scope-bound; cross-scope access is structurally impossible Layers (top → bottom) L3 Application Facade IMemoryService, MemoryServiceBuilder, query plans, eval runner L2 Retrieval Features hybrid search, fusion, reranking, corrective loop, graph retrieval, multi-representation, query plans, scope registry L1 Packages stores, vector indexes (own engine), lexical index, chunker, graph store, consolidation, correction, telemetry, eval primitives, logging L0 Types/Atoms records, results, options, contracts, primitive codecs Dependency direction: strictly downward through interfaces. No cycles. L0 — Types (ProvostXMemory.Abstractions) MemoryRecord — Id, Scope, Key, Content, Category, Tags[], Reps[], CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, ExpiresAt?, Meta MemoryScope — Kind (Platform|Session|Tenant|Purpose|Custom), Id, ParentScope?; hierarchical, immutable MemoryRepresentation — Modality (Text|Image|Table|Audio|Custom), Content, EmbeddingModelHash? ScoredMemoryRecord — Record, Score, Provenance (retriever, stage scores) RetrievalQuery — Text, Scope, TopK, Filters (tags/category/date), Plan? RetrievalResult — IReadOnlyList , Diagnostics (per-stage scores, timings) Chunk, ChunkOptions — chunk model + structural/size/overlap parameters MemoryLoggingOptions — logging/integrity/retention configuration (lives here so Abstractions stays dependency-free) QueryPlan, QueryPlanStep, QueryTokens, RetrievalProvenance, RetrievalStageDiagnostics — retrieval/pipeline atom types MemoryManifest, MemoryEntryModel — on-disk metadata codec contracts Options records: MemoryServiceOptions, StorageOptions, VectorOptions (+ IndexKind), GraphOptions, FusionOptions, ConsolidationOptions, CorrectionOptions Abstractions has ZERO project references (verified against csproj) — dependency-free atom layer. L1 — Packages (each = its own csproj + tests) Storage (ProvostXMemory.Storage) IMemoryStore — Add/Update/Delete/Get/List/Count(scope), Snapshot(scope) IJsonlMemoryStore : IMemoryStore — default store impl (JsonlMemoryStore: JSONL, transactional rewrites) IMemoryManifestCodec — manifest read/write (MemoryManifestCodec) MemoryRootLayout — root folder + scope path resolution (root/scopeKind/scopeId/modelHash) AtomicFileWriter — temp + atomic swap (POSIX-safe move, temp cleanup on failure) VectorIndex (ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex) IVectorIndex — Build(items), Add, Remove, Search(vector, k) → ScoredIds; Dim; Count; Flush IVectorIndexFactory — creates Flat/Ivf/Hnsw indexes (own engine); IndexKind enum = Flat | Ivf | Hnsw | Gpu IVectorIndexGuard — per-index dim/epoch guard (rejects stale writes across rebuilds) IVectorEmbedder — Embed(text) → float[] (host-injected) ScoredVectorId, VectorItem, VectorItemStore, VectorScanner, VectorTopKBuffer — index primitives VectorNamespaceFile — per-scope/model-hash index file format + model-hash/dim guard FlatJsonVectorIndex — zero-dependency brute-force cosine backend, transactional JSON file ScalarVectorOps, VectorMath — SIMD math (Vector512 → Vector256 → Vector128 → scalar fallback; zero-vector guarded) KMeansQuantizer, SeededRandom — deterministic k-means + locked xorshift RNG VectorIndex.Engine (ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine) — the OWN engine (no third-party vector deps): FlatExactIndex — SIMD exact brute-force scan IvfFlatIndex — k-means coarse quantizer + inverted lists (deterministic, empty-cluster reseating) HnswIndex/HnswBuilder/HnswBeamSearcher — immutable-index + batch-rebuild semantics (see Patent notes) VectorIndex.Gpu (ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu, optional) ILGPU 1.5.3 kernels (Flat + IVF): GpuFlatIndex, GpuIvfIndex, one-thread-per-slot, chunked launches, no barriers/shared memory → bit-identical accumulation order CPU/GPU IGpuAccelerator availability gate — lazy, exception-guarded; transparent injected-CPU fallback; no Engine-package reference Lexical (ProvostXMemory.Lexical) ILexicalIndex — Build/IncrementalAdd/Remove/EnumerateDocuments/Search(terms, k) → ScoredIds IBm25Scorer — saturated-TF IDF scoring + key boost Chunking (ProvostXMemory.Chunking) IChunker — Split(record, options) → Chunk[] (SizeChunker, StructuredChunker) IParentResolver — chunk id → parent record (parent-document recall) ChunkIdCodec — chunk id codec; rejects | in scope/record ids loudly (silent dense-recall loss otherwise) Fusion (ProvostXMemory.Fusion) IResultFuser — Fuse(ranked lists, weights) → fused ranked list (ReciprocalRankFuser, RRF k=60, weighted, deterministic tie order) Reranking (ProvostXMemory.Reranking) IReranker — Rerank(query, candidates) → reranked (ScoreBoostReranker additive, no drops; NoopReranker) IRerankerClient — external rerank service contract (ClientBackedReranker) Graph (ProvostXMemory.Graph) IMemoryGraphStore — UpsertEntity/UpsertRelation/Neighbors/ShortestPath/ClusterOf (JsonlMemoryGraphStore, scope-pinned) IEntityExtractor — Extract(records) → entities+relations (host-injected; HeuristicEntityExtractor default) IGraphRetriever — Retrieve(query, scope) → records + cluster summaries (GraphRetriever, deterministic BFS) GraphIndexLedger — facade-side graph extraction ledger Correction (ProvostXMemory.Correction) IRetrievalGrader — Grade(query, candidate) → Relevant/Irrelevant/Uncertain (host-injected) IQueryRewriter — Rewrite(query) → expanded/keyword query (KeywordQueryRewriter default) CorrectiveRetriever — grade→external-fetch-hook→rewrite loop via injected IExternalFetcher (bounded retries) Consolidation (ProvostXMemory.Consolidation) IMemoryConsolidator — pass over scope: dedup, TTL expiry, cluster summary emission (MemoryConsolidator) IDedupDetector (ThresholdDedupDetector) — near-duplicate detection (oldest kept, tags unioned) IClusterSummarizer — summarize cluster into a summary record Telemetry (ProvostXMemory.Telemetry) IMemoryTelemetry — query timings, per-stage scores, backend stats (host sink; NoopMemoryTelemetry/InMemoryMemoryTelemetry) Eval (ProvostXMemory.Eval) — deterministic evaluation primitives EvalCase/EvalCaseSet/DeterministicEvalCorpus — reproducible golden corpora ClusterHashEmbedder — deterministic hash embedder (no real model anywhere) EvalMetrics/EvalMetricMath — Recall@k, Precision@k, MRR, NDCG@k + per-scope/per-stage breakdowns EvalReport/EvalReportJson/EvalMetricThresholds — serializable results + threshold gates Eval references only Abstractions + VectorIndex (downward only) Logging (ProvostXMemory.Logging) — leaf package (depends only on Abstractions) IMemoryLogSink + ConsoleMemoryLogSink/FileMemoryLogSink — rolling files, JSON lines or text MemoryLogger — facade-facing logger (toggle/level via MemoryLoggingOptions) HashChainAppender/LogChainVerifier — SHA-256 hash-chain integrity (covers timestamp+seq+content+prev-hash; serialized under a gate — concurrent writes never interleave chain links) RetentionSweeper — deletes log files past the retention window (pattern-scoped deletes) L2 — Retrieval Features (ProvostXMemory.Retrieval) IHybridRetriever → HybridRetriever — dense + lexical in parallel → IResultFuser → resolve → optional IReranker (exactly ONE rerank pass; per-stage diagnostics) ICorrectiveRetriever — grader-gated hybrid retrieval with rewrite loop (Correction package) IMultiRepresentationRetriever → MultiRepresentationRetriever — query across modalities (repr|<recordId>|<index> ids; representation ids reject the separator loudly) IQueryPlanRunner → QueryPlanRunner — executes declarative QueryPlan: target-scope fan-out, scope-qualified fusion ids (same record id in two scopes never conflates), weak-evidence single rewrite-retry IScopeIndexRegistry → InMemoryScopeIndexRegistry — scope-exact artifact registry (vector/lexical/record provider per scope; exact-scope keys) L3 — Application Facade (ProvostXMemory root package) IMemoryService — THE public surface: RememberAsync/ForgetAsync/UpdateAsync — store + dense/lexical index maintenance via per-record id ledger; optional graph extraction RecallAsync(RetrievalQuery) → RetrievalResult — routes: plan → corrective (when grader wired) → hybrid → optional rerank (single rerank pass) ConsolidateAsync(scope, options) — delegates to IMemoryConsolidator, refreshes/removes index artifacts BuildIndexesAsync(scope)/RebuildAsync — chunk + embed + vector + lexical build per scope Scopes() — enumerate existing scopes (IScopesAware store hook, directory-layout fallback) MemoryService — composition root; takes MemoryServiceOptions + injected deps MemoryServiceBuilder — fluent wiring helper (still DI, no service locator) EvalRunner + DefaultEvalServiceFactory live HERE (they compose a full IMemoryService; keeps Eval a pure L1 — no L1→L3 edge) RootChildScopeResolver, MemoryServicePipelineOptions, RetrievalFilterApplier Backend matrix Backend Package Notes FlatJson (default) core zero-dependency brute-force cosine, transactional JSON file FlatExact (SIMD) …VectorIndex.Engine own engine, Vector512 kernels, exact search IvfFlat …VectorIndex.Engine own engine, deterministic k-means coarse quantizer + inverted lists Hnsw …VectorIndex.Engine own engine, immutable-index + batch-rebuild semantics Gpu (ILGPU, optional) …VectorIndex.Gpu own kernels (Flat + IVF), lazy guarded availability, transparent CPU fallback (bit-identical results) Native FAISS (P/Invoke) not adopted own engine replaces it; zero third-party vector deps All backends pass the SAME IVectorIndex conformance suite; cross-backend parity and determinism pinned by tests. Concurrency & correctness model Per-service async store gate (SemaphoreSlim): store write + index mutation + graph update serialize across Remember/Forget/Update; embeddings compute OUTSIDE the gate (parallel-safe) Per-service lexical mutation gate: lexical index (plain Dictionary) mutations never race readers Serialized hash-chain logging gate: concurrent log entries never interleave chain links Index guard (IVectorIndexGuard): dim/epoch mismatched (stale, post-rebuild) writes rejected loudly Everything else audited clean (three full-context audits 2026-10-13): no races beyond the gates above, no leaks (scope isolation structurally enforced), no unhandled IO paths, all traversals hop-bounded/visited-guarded Dependency flow MemoryService (L3) → IHybridRetriever/ICorrectiveRetriever/IQueryPlanRunner (L2) → IFusion/ILexical/IVectorIndex/IMemoryGraphStore/IRetrievalGrader (L1) → IMemoryStore + record types (L0) Abstractions (L0): zero references Eval (L1): Abstractions + VectorIndex only, downward VectorIndex.Gpu: VectorIndex interfaces only (CPU fallback index injected) — no Engine reference Logging (L1): leaf, Abstractions only Facade (L3): references Eval (runner/factory composition) + all backend packages Hosts reference ONLY the root package + optionally backend packages Storage layout (per root folder, host-configured) <root>/ manifest.json <scope-kind>/<scope-id>/ records.jsonl chunks/ vectors/<model-hash>/index.json (FlatJson backend) graph/entities.jsonl, relations.jsonl, clusters.jsonl Testing strategy One test project per package (17 suites) + ProvostXMemory.SystemTests — host-agnostic: zero references to any product; exercises ONLY the public surface with ClusterHashEmbedder + temp-dir store Tiers: UNIT (scope/filters/chunker/fuser/HNSW-determinism/report round-trip), INTEGRATION (backend matrix parity: FlatExact/Ivf/Hnsw/FlatJson/Gpu-fallback — identical deterministic rankings cross-backend; persistence/restart; consolidation; graph clusters), JOURNEY (knowledge assistant Recall@5 ≥ 0.9 — achieved 1.0; multi-tenant 3-scope isolation, zero leakage incl. restart; lifecycle) 5 real concurrency/durability bugs found by audits and pinned by regression tests: hash-chain gate, ChunkIdCodec pipe rejection, facade double-rerank removal, lexical mutation gate, store gate Suite total: 626 green, 0 warnings / 0 errors on .NET 8 Known semantics (documented decisions, not bugs) QueryPlanRunnerOptions.WeakEvidenceThreshold (default 0.02) is on the RRF scale: with a rewriter wired, pass-2 (rewritten) fully REPLACES pass-1 when the top hit lacks two-stage corroboration — retry-only-when-uncorroborated semantics JsonlMemoryStore.WriteEntryAsync appends replaced entries at file end while UpdateAsync preserves position — both full rewrites; consumers re-sort Cold-index semantics: recall on a fresh MemoryService over an existing root is empty until BuildIndexesAsync/RebuildAsync Patent & license notes (own engine) Owner decision (2026-10-13): build our own FAISS-equivalent in C#; ALL third-party vector-index packages dropped (Gravicode.FaissNet unverified license; FAISS ships no .NET bindings) Patent review: NO broad granted patent on HNSW core (build + greedy layered search). Sole known claim = US application 15/929,802 "Dynamic Updates for HNSW" (narrow: incremental updates on live graphs, pending). Our HNSW uses immutable built indexes + batch rebuild on mutation — it never implements the claimed dynamic-update method. IVF/Flat = classic methods, no blocking claims. Earlier "Yandex HNSW patent" note was wrong (unrelated number) — corrected. ILGPU 1.5.3: NCSA license (MIT-compatible), verified against the license file shipped in the nupkg — see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md Periodic HNSW patent-status re-check: owner-gated backlog item (see docs/BACKLOG-MASTER.md) Documentation artifacts README.md — landing (features, quickstart, backend matrix, design principles) docs/ — getting-started, concepts, scopes, retrieval, backends, consolidation, evaluation, logging, api-glossary, FAQ docs/api-site/ — DocFX API reference (265 pages), generated from the shared corporate template (~/Agent/ProvostX/docs/templates/docfx-template/) docs/wiki.html — single-file offline wiki browser (generated by .ldc/gen_wiki.py) API-INDEX.md / RELATIONSHIP-GRAPH.md / PACKAGE-MAP.md — LDC artifacts (generated by .ldc/gen_ldc.py) docs/BACKLOG-MASTER.md — owner-gated backlog (NuGet publish, Inference-backed embedder adapter, HNSW patent re-check)

CONCEPT.html.title: ProvostXMemory — Concept | ProvostXMemory API
CONCEPT.html.summary: ProvostXMemory — Concept License: MIT. What it is A standalone .NET library that owns ALL memory and retrieval concerns for any host application (Agent satellite, Admin platform, future products). Hosts see one clean surface (IMemoryService + options) and never know what storage, indexing, or retrieval strategy is running underneath. Swappable by config, nothing else. What problem it solves Every ProvostX project ends up re-implementing retrieval (the old Agent rolled its own flat-JSON vector index + BM25-lite; the Knowledge repo has FAISS + a shell script). Memory logic should live in ONE atomic, encapsulated library: Hosts reference one NuGet package, wire it via constructor injection, done Backends (flat JSON, FAISS, sqlite-vec) are pluggable — chosen by config Multi-tenant isolation: memory is separated by platform / session / tenant / purpose via namespaces. Different users, sessions, or products NEVER see each other's memories Full retrieval stack: chunking, hybrid lexical+vector search, fusion, reranking, corrective loops, graph traversal, multi-representation records Core capabilities (RAG architecture coverage) Hybrid retrieval: BM25 lexical + dense vector search with RRF/weighted fusion Chunking policies: structural/size/overlap chunking + parent-document recall Graph layer: entities + relations over memory records; subgraph retrieval, cluster summaries Corrective loop: retrieval evaluator hook (grade → keep / web-out / rewrite query) — grader injected by host, library stays LLM-agnostic Agentic surface: retrieval as a declarative query-plan (fan out namespaces, merge, iterate on weak evidence) Multi-representation records: one record, many representations (text / image caption / table), per-modality embeddings in one namespace Backend matrix FlatJson — zero-dependency default (ported from the old Agent; brute-force cosine) FaissManaged — pure-.NET FAISS port (Gravicode.FaissNet), CPU SIMD FaissGpu — ILGPU (CUDA/OpenCL) with CPU fallback, later tier Native FAISS dylib matrix via P/Invoke — optional, only if managed port falls short Isolation model Root folder per host install; inside it, namespace segments: <root>/<scope-kind>/<scope-id>/<model-hash>/… Scope kinds: platform (telegram/discord/…), session, tenant, custom purpose. Every store/index/graph operation is scope-bound; cross-scope reads are impossible by construction, not by convention. Who uses it Hosts that need durable, recallable memory: the Agent satellite (sessions, curated memory), Admin platform (tenant search), any future product. Integration cost: one package reference + a few config lines + DI wiring. Non-goals Hosting web search itself (hosts provide external fetchers via interface) Choosing embedding models (hosts inject IVectorEmbedder; library validates hashes/dims) UI of any kind

README.html.title: ProvostXMemory | ProvostXMemory API
README.html.summary: ProvostXMemory A strict-OOP, host-agnostic long-term memory library for .NET — scoped storage, hybrid (dense + lexical) retrieval with enforced filters, consolidation, graph, corrective recall, an eval harness, and audit-grade integrity-logged observability — over pluggable vector-index backends with an own C# engine and zero third-party vector dependencies. License MIT (LICENSE) Target .NET 8 Tests 626 green (xUnit, 17 suites), 0 warnings / 0 errors Native dependencies None (pure managed; ILGPU ships in the package — GPU acceleration included, transparent CPU fallback) Why ProvostXMemory One facade. Hosts see IMemoryService + typed options and inject their own embedder, grader, reranker, and telemetry. Storage, indexing, and retrieval strategy are swappable by configuration — never by host code changes. Scope-isolated by construction. Memory is partitioned per scope (platform / session / tenant / purpose / custom), and cross-scope access is structurally impossible — enforced by path layout and scope-exact registries, pinned by dedicated tests, not by convention. Own vector engine, zero native deps. Flat (SIMD Vector512), IVF, and HNSW are implemented in C#; the included ILGPU kernels accelerate Flat/IVF on the GPU when an accelerator is present and fall back to the CPU bit-identically otherwise. No FAISS, no native dylibs, no server. Features Area What you get Key types Storage Transactional JSONL records per scope, manifests, atomic writes IMemoryStore, JsonlMemoryStore, MemoryRootLayout, AtomicFileWriter Vector index Pluggable backends with a shared conformance suite IVectorIndex, IVectorIndexFactory, IndexKind Lexical BM25-lite inverted index with key boosts ILexicalIndex, Bm25Scorer Fusion RRF fusion with dense/lexical weights IResultFuser, ReciprocalRankFuser Retrieval Hybrid, corrective loop, graph, multi-representation, declarative query plans, enforced filters IHybridRetriever, ICorrectiveRetriever, IGraphRetriever, IMultiRepresentationRetriever, IQueryPlanRunner Chunking Structural and size/overlap chunking with parent-document recall IChunker, StructuredChunker, IParentResolver Graph Entities, relations, shortest path, cluster summaries IMemoryGraphStore, IEntityExtractor, GraphRetriever Consolidation Dedup, TTL expiry, cluster summaries IMemoryConsolidator, IDedupDetector, IClusterSummarizer Reranking Heuristic or client-backed reranking IReranker, ScoreBoostReranker, ClientBackedReranker Correction Grader-gated retrieval with query rewrite loop IRetrievalGrader, IQueryRewriter, CorrectiveRetriever Evaluation Recall@k / Precision@k / MRR / NDCG, thresholds, regression guard, JSON reports EvalRunner, EvalMetricMath, DeterministicEvalCorpus Logging Configurable sinks, SHA-256 audit hash chain, retention, content minimization MemoryLoggingOptions, LogChainVerifier, RetentionSweeper Telemetry Per-stage timings and scores into a host sink IMemoryTelemetry Quickstart using ProvostXMemory; using ProvostXMemory.Abstractions; using ProvostXMemory.Fusion; using ProvostXMemory.Storage; using ProvostXMemory.Telemetry; using ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine; var root = "/data/memory-root"; var layout = new MemoryRootLayout(root, "model-hash-v1"); IMemoryService memory = new MemoryServiceBuilder() .WithOptions(new MemoryServiceOptions( Storage: new StorageOptions(root), Vector: new VectorOptions("model-hash-v1", dim: 768, IndexKind.IndexKind.Hnsw), Graph: GraphOptions.Default, Fusion: new FusionOptions(), Consolidation: new ConsolidationOptions())) .WithStore(new JsonlMemoryStore(layout)) .WithEmbedder(embedder) // host-injected IVectorEmbedder .WithIndexFactory(new EngineVectorIndexFactory()) .WithFuser(new ReciprocalRankFuser()) .WithTelemetry(NoopMemoryTelemetry.Instance) .Build(); var scope = new MemoryScope(MemoryScopeKind.Session, "user-42"); await memory.RememberAsync(new MemoryRecord( "note-1", scope, "helm-rollout", "Kubernetes rollout notes…", Category: "ops", Tags: new[] { "infra", "deploy" })); await memory.BuildIndexesAsync(scope); RetrievalResult result = await memory.RecallAsync(new RetrievalQuery( "kubernetes rollout", scope, TopK: 5, Filters: new RetrievalFilters(Tags: new[] { "deploy" }))); foreach (var hit in result.Records) { Console.WriteLine($"{hit.Score:0.000} {hit.Record.Id}: {hit.Record.Key}"); } Backend matrix Backend Package Exactness Scale guidance Notes FlatJson (default) core exact up to a few thousand vectors per scope brute-force cosine, transactional JSON persistence, zero deps FlatExact (SIMD) ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine exact up to ~10k per scope Vector512 kernels, own engine IVF ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine approximate (tunable nprobe) 10k–1M deterministic k-means quantizer + inverted lists HNSW ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine approximate 10k–10M immutable built indexes + batch rebuild; measured recall@10 = 0.998 GPU (ILGPU) ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu exact (Flat, IVF) Flat/IVF scale lazy guarded availability; transparent CPU fallback with bit-identical results Select via VectorOptions.IndexKind (Flat | Ivf | Hnsw | Gpu) plus the matching IVectorIndexFactory; every backend passes the same conformance suite. Details in docs/backends.md. Retrieval pipeline RetrievalQuery ──► routing (plan → corrective → hybrid → rerank) │ dense vector ┴─ lexical BM25 (per scope, in parallel) │ RRF fusion (weights, k=60) │ resolve ids → records (parent-document recall, multi-representation) │ filter enforcement (tags / category / date window) │ optional rerank ──► corrective loop (grade → rewrite → retry) │ RetrievalResult + per-stage diagnostics Logging and audit hash-chain Logging is off by default with zero cost. When enabled it offers file/console/injected sinks, JSON-lines format, rotation, retention, strict content minimization (IncludeContent = false — record content never appears in logs), and a SHA-256 hash chain that makes any tampering, deletion, or reordering of historical entries verifiable via LogChainVerifier. See docs/logging.md. Evaluation harness ProvostXMemory.Eval measures Recall@k, Precision@k, MRR, and NDCG over golden query sets against deterministic corpora, checks metric thresholds as a regression guard, and emits canonical diff-friendly JSON reports. The library's own journey tests gate on Recall@5 ≥ 0.9 (achieved 1.0). See docs/evaluation.md. The library knows nothing about its hosts; hosts know nothing about the internals. No environment variables — all configuration is typed options. All file I/O is transactional (temp + atomic swap). Every backend passes the same conformance suite; cross-backend parity and determinism are pinned by tests. License Licensed under the MIT License. api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.Consolid.summary: Class ConsolidationOptions Tuning for one IMemoryService.ConsolidateAsync pass over a scope. DedupSimilarityThreshold — cosine above which two records count as near-duplicates (lexical Jaccard fallback when embeddings degenerate). The OLDEST record of each duplicate group is kept, tags are unioned into it, the rest are deleted. ExpireTtl — when on (default), records whose ExpiresAt is past are deleted first. EmitClusterSummaries — when on, the remaining near-duplicate clusters (similarity ≥ the ConsolidationTuning.ClusterJoinThreshold) emit one summary record each, graph-recorded when a graph extractor is wired. api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IMemoryS.title: Interface IMemoryStore | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IMemoryS.summary: Interface IMemoryStore The durable record store seam. Every method takes the scope explicitly (kind + id) — there is no scope-less operation anywhere in the contract, so a store implementation physically cannot conflate scopes. The default JsonlMemoryStore lays out one records.jsonl per scope directory with transactional rewrites (temp file + atomic move) and tolerant reads (blank lines and legacy entries without Reps/Meta deserialize to defaults). Concurrency contract: implementations are not required to be internally thread-safe — IMemoryService serializes store mutations per service instance; direct multi-threaded store access is the host's own synchronization problem. api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IndexKin.title: Enum IndexKind | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.IndexKin.summary: Enum IndexKind The vector index backend family. Flat — exact SIMD scan, the correctness baseline and the best choice up to tens of thousands of vectors. Ivf — deterministic k-means inverted lists; probes only nprobe clusters per query, the sweet spot for large corpora. Hnsw — navigable-small-world graph, highest recall per query latency; built with immutable-index/rebuild semantics and searched with a layered greedy beam (see the architecture patent addendum). Gpu — ILGPU-kernel decoration over a CPU backend with bit-exact fallback when no device exists. All kinds pass one shared conformance suite; results are interchangeable between kinds (FlatJson included, see IVectorIndex). api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemoryLo.summary: Class MemoryLoggingOptions Logging configuration for the memory service. Off by default — Enabled = false means zero writes, zero log-entry allocations on the hot path, no log directory created. Enabled logging is content-minimized: log lines carry what happened (scope, operation, scores, durations), never record content itself, unless IncludeContent is explicitly set — the default-persisted posture is behavior-evidence without user-content retention. Audit mode: Integrity = MemoryLogIntegrity.HashChain appends entries SHA-256 hash-chained to their predecessor (with monotonic sequence numbers) under a serialized gate — any modified or deleted line breaks verification, and LogChainVerifier proves integrity in one pass. api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.MemorySc.summary: Class MemoryScope One isolation boundary of memory: the (Kind, Id) pair every record, index, and log line belongs to. Records written to one scope are structurally invisible to operations on another — the storage root layout pins each scope to its own directory tree and the index registry keys indexes by the exact scope pair. Scopes may carry a ParentScope chain for hierarchical fan-out (query plans target a root and resolve child scopes), but lookups never fall through to parents: a query against scope A sees scope A, nothing else, whatever its ancestry. api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.html.title: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Abstractions | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Abstractions.html.summary: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Abstractions Classes BackendStats Stats snapshot of a backend (store or index). Chunk A chunk produced by splitting a memory record. StartOffset and EndOffset are half-open offsets into the parent record's content (parentContent[StartOffset..EndOffset] == Content); the value -1 means "unset". Chunkers always set both. ChunkOptions Chunking parameters: structural markers, size and overlap. A trailing chunk shorter than MinChunkLength merges into its predecessor (may exceed the max — max is a packing target, min is a hard floor). ConsolidationOptions Tuning for one IMemoryService.ConsolidateAsync pass over a scope. DedupSimilarityThreshold — cosine above which two records count as near-duplicates (lexical Jaccard fallback when embeddings degenerate). The OLDEST record of each duplicate group is kept, tags are unioned into it, the rest are deleted. ExpireTtl — when on (default), records whose ExpiresAt is past are deleted first. EmitClusterSummaries — when on, the remaining near-duplicate clusters (similarity ≥ the ConsolidationTuning.ClusterJoinThreshold) emit one summary record each, graph-recorded when a graph extractor is wired. FusionOptions Fusion options: RRF constant and stage weights. GraphOptions Graph layer options: neighbor fan-out cap, walk depth, retriever behavior knobs. MemoryEntryModel Logical record model as persisted on disk (JSONL entry shape). Reps and Meta are optional trailing parameters: entries written before they existed (or writers that leave them out) deserialize with null, which the store maps to the record's empty defaults — never a null crash. MemoryLoggingOptions Logging configuration for the memory service. Off by default — Enabled = false means zero writes, zero log-entry allocations on the hot path, no log directory created. Enabled logging is content-minimized: log lines carry what happened (scope, operation, scores, durations), never record content itself, unless IncludeContent is explicitly set — the default-persisted posture is behavior-evidence without user-content retention. Audit mode: Integrity = MemoryLogIntegrity.HashChain appends entries SHA-256 hash-chained to their predecessor (with monotonic sequence numbers) under a serialized gate — any modified or deleted line breaks verification, and LogChainVerifier proves integrity in one pass. RetentionDays triggers the retention sweeper; both file and console sinks are available, hosts inject their own IMemoryLogSink (SIEM, Serilog, …) through the builder. MemoryManifest On-disk metadata describing the memory root: codecs, counts, versions. MemoryRecord The unit of remembered knowledge: an immutable record with identity, scope, content, and retrieval hints. Records are created by hosts and persisted through IMemoryService.RememberAsync; retrieval returns them wrapped in ScoredMemoryRecord. Retrieval relevance is driven by Content (embedded and lexically indexed), boosted by Tags and Key terms and Category exact matches in the default reranker. Optional Reps add per-modality content (image captions, tables) that is embedded alongside the text and retrievable through the multi-representation retriever. MemoryRepresentation Additional per-modality content of a record: image captions, tables, audio transcripts, or any parallel content that should be retrievable alongside the record's main text. Each representation is embedded with the host's IVectorEmbedder and indexed under its own vector id (repr|<recordId>|<index>); the multi-representation retriever compares a query against every representation and keeps the best-matching one per record. Modality contract: Modality is a tag, not a type system — content is always string. EmbeddingModelHash is optional metadata for hosts that run several embedding models; the vector index namespace guard keys on the model hash + dimension, not on this field. MemoryScope One isolation boundary of memory: the (Kind, Id) pair every record, index, and log line belongs to. Records written to one scope are structurally invisible to operations on another — the storage root layout pins each scope to its own directory tree and the index registry keys indexes by the exact scope pair. Scopes may carry a ParentScope chain for hierarchical fan-out (query plans target a root and resolve child scopes), but lookups never fall through to parents: a query against scope A sees scope A, nothing else, whatever its ancestry. MemoryServiceOptions The root options record for MemoryService: the host's per-domain tuning, injected once at build time. Each section covers one pipeline concern — Storage (root layout), Vector (backend + dim), Graph (walk tuning), Fusion (RRF weights), Consolidation (dedup/cluster thresholds), Logging Section records carry safe defaults; a host that passes all defaults gets the reference pipeline. Optional capabilities (grader, graph extractor, reranker, log sink) are injected via MemoryServiceBuilder rather than this record — options tune behavior, wiring enables capabilities. QueryPlan Declarative retrieval plan: an ordered set of steps the runner executes. QueryPlanStep One step of a declarative plan (fan-out namespaces, merge, iterate). QueryTokens Pure query-text token helpers shared by text-processing packages (keyword rewriting, score-boost reranking). Stateless lookups and a compiled regex only; this class is the architecture-sanctioned pure-function static: no I/O, no ambient state, deterministic. RetrievalFilters Immutable tag/category/date filter set for retrieval. RetrievalProvenance Provenance of a scored memory record: which retriever produced it and per-stage scores. RetrievalQuery A scope-bound retrieval request: what to look for, where to look, and how much to return. Passed to IMemoryService.RecallAsync. Scope is authoritative — results are drawn from that scope's indexes only, never from other scopes. Text runs through the full pipeline (embedding + BM25 lexical + fusion + optional rerank/corrective loop); an empty or whitespace text short-circuits to an empty result. TopK bounds the returned records. Filters (tags, category, date-from) are applied after fusion, so they never affect ranking of the candidates they admit. Plan (when set) executes a declarative multi-scope fan-out instead of a single-scope lookup — see QueryPlanRunner. RetrievalResult The outcome of IMemoryService.RecallAsync: the scored records, best first, plus per-stage diagnostics. Records is ordered by Score descending with deterministic tie-breaks by record id. Diagnostics carries one entry per pipeline stage (dense, lexical, fusion, rerank, corrective retries) with durations and stage-specific metrics — feed it to the eval harness for Recall@k/MRR/NDCG. RetrievalStageDiagnostics Diagnostics of one retrieval stage (scores and timing). ScoredId A scored hit from a store/index search: scope kind, scope id, id, score. ScoredMemoryRecord A record matched by a retrieval, its relevance score, and where the score came from. Provenance names the stage that produced the score and carries per-stage subscores (e.g. the fused RRF score plus the rerank-adjusted score), so ranking changes across pipeline stages remain explainable end to end. StorageOptions FlatJson store options: root folder + durability settings. VectorOptions Vector index options: backend kind, model hash, dimension, default top-k. Interfaces IJsonlMemoryStore Default JSONL-backed store contract (transactional file I/O). IMemoryManifestCodec Manifest read/write for a memory root. IMemoryStore The durable record store seam. Every method takes the scope explicitly (kind + id) — there is no scope-less operation anywhere in the contract, so a store implementation physically cannot conflate scopes. The default JsonlMemoryStore lays out one records.jsonl per scope directory with transactional rewrites (temp file + atomic move) and tolerant reads (blank lines and legacy entries without Reps/Meta deserialize to defaults). Concurrency contract: implementations are not required to be internally thread-safe — IMemoryService serializes store mutations per service instance; direct multi-threaded store access is the host's own synchronization problem. Enums IndexKind The vector index backend family. Flat — exact SIMD scan, the correctness baseline and the best choice up to tens of thousands of vectors. Ivf — deterministic k-means inverted lists; probes only nprobe clusters per query, the sweet spot for large corpora. Hnsw — navigable-small-world graph, highest recall per query latency; built with immutable-index/rebuild semantics and searched with a layered greedy beam (see the architecture patent addendum). Gpu — ILGPU-kernel decoration over a CPU backend with bit-exact fallback when no device exists. All kinds pass one shared conformance suite; results are interchangeable between kinds (FlatJson included, see IVectorIndex). MemoryLogFormat Seriline format used by the file sink. MemoryLogIntegrity Integrity protection applied to log entries. MemoryLogLevel Severity of a memory log entry. MemoryLogSinkKind Where log entries are written. MemoryRepresentationModality Modality of a memory representation. MemoryScopeKind The isolation axis of a MemoryScope. One record lives in exactly one (Kind, Id) pair; the kind determines what the id conventionally names: Platform (one surface — e.g. per chat platform), Session (one conversation or run), Tenant (one customer — multi-tenant hosts), Purpose (one knowledge base or domain), Custom (host-defined). Kinds map to storage path segments, so cross-kind and cross-id isolation are identical by construction. Unknown on-disk kinds degrade to Custom on read.

api/ProvostXMemory.Chunking.IChunker.htm.title: Interface IChunker | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Chunking.IChunker.htm.summary: Interface IChunker Splits a record's content into embedded units for the dense index. Chunks carry exact offsets back into the original content, so a chunk hit resolves to its parent record — the whole record is always what surfaces in results, never the fragment. Implementations: StructuredChunker cuts on markdown structure first (headings, paragraphs, then sentences) and only hard-slices oversized content; SizeChunker packs by size with optional overlap — fixed-stride windows in geometry mode, shared whole words in separator mode. Both preserve every character of content across the split (mod whitespace at cut points). Chunk ids are scope-qualified (kind|scope-id|record-id|index) — see ChunkIdCodec; ids containing the '|' separator are rejected at compose time. api/ProvostXMemory.Chunking.SizeChunker..title: Class SizeChunker | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Chunking.SizeChunker..summary: Class SizeChunker Pure size + overlap splitting for unstructured content. Two modes: geometry (no separator): with Overlap = 0 content is cut at separators (paragraph break → newline → sentence terminator → hard slice of exactly max) with separator whitespace consumed at cuts; with overlap > 0 fixed stride windows (stride = max − overlap, window = max) guarantee consecutive chunks share exactly Overlap characters and no character is lost. Separator mode: words are packed and joined by the separator; Overlap counts shared whole words repeated from the previous chunk's tail (rolling window), so shared text matches word for word. api/ProvostXMemory.Consolidation.MemoryC.summary: Class MemoryConsolidator One consolidation pass over a scope, executed against the scope-bound IMemoryStore: (1) TTL expiry deletes records whose ExpiresAt is in the past, (2) near-duplicate detection via IDedupDetector keeps the oldest record of each duplicate group and unions the tags of the removed duplicates into the kept record, (3) remaining records are clustered by embedding similarity and clusters of sufficient size are emitted as summary records via IClusterSummarizer, (4) all mutations are counted in a ConsolidationReport attached to the returned records. Survivors and summaries are returned (survivors first, summaries last); an empty scope is a no-op returning an empty list. Every deletion goes through the store's scope-bound API — cross-scope access stays structurally impossible. api/ProvostXMemory.Eval.html.title: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Eval | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Eval.html.summary: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Eval Classes ClusterHashEmbedder Deterministic fake embedder for eval runs — NOT a real model. Cluster-preserving: every token maps to a fixed slot from a stable FNV-1a hash; each of a record's tokens adds a fixed cluster id + token hash signature so similar content (shared cluster terms) lands near the same direction, with per-record seeded noise amplitude only. No randomness at embed time: same text → same vector, always. DeterministicEvalCorpus Seeded synthetic corpus: N records per scope across M scopes, round-robin assigned to keyword clusters (exact balance) so every scope/cluster pair yields the same number of expected matches per query. Content is a seeded shuffle of the record's cluster terms plus filler words, one hard-negative term from a seeded foreign cluster, and one seeded noise token — derivable relevance without an LLM: the expected matches for a cluster query are exactly that cluster's records. Identical seeds yield byte-identical corpora, verified via DeterminismHash(). DeterministicEvalCorpus.CorpusRecord EvalCase One golden retrieval case: a query bound to a scope plus the record ids a good retriever should surface. Relevance is binary (1.0) unless graded weights are given. The query's TopK is overridden by the eval runner options' TopK at run time. EvalCaseMetrics Metrics for one eval case: Recall@k, Precision@k, MRR and NDCG@k over the ranked result ids judged against the case's golden relevance. EvalCaseSet A named set of golden eval cases grouped under one logical set id. Case ids must be unique within a scope (cross-scope ids may repeat); the set is immutable after creation. EvalCaseTrace Per-case ranked outcome: returned ids with their graded relevance gains and how many returned records came from a scope other than the case's own (isolation guard). EvalCaseTraceHit One returned id with its graded relevance gain for this case. EvalMetricBreakdownEntry Metric means for a breakdown group (scope or retriever stage). EvalMetricMath The metric formulas, implemented independently of any search engine and unit-tested against hand-computed values: Recall@k = |relevant ∩ top-k| / |relevant| (0 when no relevant ids). Precision@k = |relevant ∩ top-k| / k (unfilled top-k counts against precision). MRR = 1 / rank of the first relevant hit, else 0. NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k with DCG = Σ relᵢ / log₂(rank + 1), rank starting at 1. All instance methods (no static state shared across instances). EvalMetricThresholds Minimum metric values for the aggregate EvalReport. A violation is any actual value strictly below its threshold. All thresholds optional (null = unchecked). EvalMetrics Aggregate over all cases: plain means of the per-case metric values. EvalReport Serializable result of running an EvalCaseSet: per-case metrics, the aggregate, per-scope and per-stage breakdowns, threshold violations, and the per-case ranked id lists (with graded gains) for diffing. JSON-ready via System.Text.Json. EvalReportJson JSON (de)serialization for EvalReport (System.Text.Json). MemoryScopeComparer Ordinal scope comparison helper (Kind + Id); shared by eval components. MetricThresholdViolation One threshold violation: metric name, actual vs required. MetricThresholdViolations Immutable violation list; empty when all thresholds pass.

api/ProvostXMemory.Graph.html.title: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Graph | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Graph.html.summary: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Graph Classes ExtractionResult Entity + relation extraction result. GraphCluster A graph cluster (community) with an optional summary record id. GraphEntity An extracted graph entity. EntityId is the stable slug id; Name is the canonical display form; Aliases holds alternative spellings/casings; RecordIds lists the records mentioning it. GraphRelation A relation between two graph entities, treated as undirected for traversal. Weight is implicit: RecordIds.Count equals the number of supporting records. GraphRetriever Graph-backed retriever: lowercased query tokens are matched against entity ids and entity names/aliases (via SearchEntitiesAsync(string, int, CancellationToken)) and against record tags from the scope's snapshot; matched entities seed a multi-source neighbor walk up to MaxHops hops via NeighborsAsync(string, int, CancellationToken); records touched by discovered entities and their relations plus SummaryRecordId of matched clusters are scored by hop distance (direct evidence = 1.0, each additional hop × 0.5 decay; independent evidence sums). Entity/relation extraction is an index-time concern (IEntityExtractor); this retriever is deliberately query-time token-based. HeuristicEntityExtractor Zero-dependency heuristic extractor: capitalized multi-word phrases and keyword/tag matches become entities; entities co-occurring inside one record become relations (label "co-occurs", weight = number of supporting records). Deliberately simple default; hosts inject stronger IEntityExtractor implementations. JsonlMemoryGraphStore JSONL-backed graph store: graph/entities.jsonl, graph/relations.jsonl and graph/clusters.jsonl per scope directory (via GraphPath(string, string, string)). Paths resolve only through the layout, so cross-scope access stays structurally impossible. Every mutation rewrites the affected JSONL file transactionally via AtomicFileWriter. Interfaces IEntityExtractor Host-injected entity/relation extractor (LLM or heuristic). IGraphRetriever Retrieves records from a relevant subgraph plus cluster summaries. IMemoryGraphStore Graph-backed store over memory records: entities, relations, paths, clusters. IMemoryGraphStoreResolver Resolves the scope-pinned graph store for a memory scope. Implementations must guarantee that the returned store is bound to exactly the requested scope, so cross-scope access stays structurally impossible.

api/ProvostXMemory.GraphIndexLedger.html.summary: Class GraphIndexLedger Index-time graph maintenance over the scope-pinned IMemoryGraphStore (resolved via IMemoryGraphStoreResolver): per record, the wired IEntityExtractor's entities/relations are upserted for the record's scope only; when a record is forgotten, its mentions are dropped by re-extracting the scope's remaining snapshot. The ledger itself holds no per-record entity cache — graph stores accumulate weight by design, so Forget rebuilds the affected entity mention lists from the surviving records. Scope comes from the record; the resolver is scope-exact by contract. api/ProvostXMemory.IMemoryService.html.title: Interface IMemoryService | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.IMemoryService.html.summary: Interface IMemoryService The single public surface of the ProvostXMemory library. Host applications see this interface — plus the options records they pass to MemoryServiceBuilder — and nothing else. Every capability of the library (durable storage, hybrid lexical and dense-vector retrieval, fusion, reranking, optional corrective and graph retrieval, consolidation, and audit-grade logging) is reachable through the members below. Scope isolation. Every record belongs to exactly one MemoryScope (platform, session, tenant, purpose, or custom). Every operation is scope-bound; a record written to scope A is structurally invisible to operations on scope B — the storage layout and the index registry make cross-scope access impossible rather than merely discouraged. Concurrency. Implementations are safe for concurrent use from multiple threads. Mutations (Remember/Update/Forget) are serialized per service instance; embedding computation happens outside the serialization gate, so concurrent callers do not block on model latency. Namespace: ProvostXMemory Assembly: ProvostXMemory.dll Syntax public interface IMemoryService Remarks A MemoryService is composed via MemoryServiceBuilder: construct the service by wiring the required dependencies (store, embedder, index factory, fuser) and any optional capabilities (grader → corrective loop, graph extractor, reranker, chunker, log sink), then hold the returned IMemoryService for the lifetime of your host. Retrieval quality is observable through RetrievalResult diagnostics: every RecallAsync(RetrievalQuery, CancellationToken) returns per-stage scores and timings, which the ProvostXMemory.Eval harness turns into Recall@k / Precision@k / MRR / NDCG reports. Examples var service = new MemoryServiceBuilder() .WithOptions(options) .WithStore(store) .WithEmbedder(embedder) .WithIndexFactory(new EngineVectorIndexFactory()) .WithFuser(new ReciprocalRankFuser()) .WithTelemetry(NoopMemoryTelemetry.Instance) .Build(); var scope = new MemoryScope(MemoryScopeKind.Session, "user-42"); var fact = new MemoryRecord( Id: "fact-1", Scope: scope, Key: "api gateway", Content: "The API gateway binds on port 48321."); await service.RememberAsync(fact); var result = await service.RecallAsync(new RetrievalQuery("which port", scope, 5)); Methods BuildIndexesAsync(MemoryScope, CancellationToken) Builds the scope's indexes from the store's current snapshot (retrieval works without this when records were remembered through this service; call it after populating a store directly, or after restart). Declaration Task BuildIndexesAsync(MemoryScope scope, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters Type Name Description MemoryScope scope CancellationToken cancellationToken Returns Type Description Task ConsolidateAsync(MemoryScope, ConsolidationOptions, CancellationToken) Runs one consolidation pass over a scope: TTL expiry deletes records whose ExpiresAt is in the past, near-duplicates are detected (embeddings with a lexical fallback), the oldest record of each duplicate group is kept with the group's tags unioned in, and sufficiently large near-duplicate clusters emit a summary record. Survivors and summaries are returned as the consolidated set. Declaration Task ConsolidateAsync(MemoryScope scope, ConsolidationOptions options, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters Type Name Description MemoryScope scope ConsolidationOptions options CancellationToken cancellationToken Returns Type Description Task ForgetAsync(MemoryScope, string, CancellationToken) Removes a record from the scope's store and every index (vector, lexical, graph). Declaration Task ForgetAsync(MemoryScope scope, string id, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters Type Name Description MemoryScope scope string id CancellationToken cancellationToken Returns Type Description Task Remarks Idempotent: forgetting an unknown id completes without error. Scope comes from the query; results never cross scopes. api/ProvostXMemory.Lexical.ILexicalIndex.summary: Interface ILexicalIndex The lexical half of hybrid retrieval: a BM25-weighted inverted index over record text, kept in sync by the memory service (records remember/update → IncrementalAdd; forget → Remove). Complements the dense stage by matching exact terms embeddings miss (identifiers, acronyms, version numbers); both stages fuse into one ranking via IResultFuser. Contract: tokens are lowercase alphanumeric words (no stemming, no external NLP); scores are saturated-TF × IDF with a key-match boost. The index itself is not thread-safe — the memory service serializes all mutations; external callers must not share an instance unsynchronized. api/ProvostXMemory.Lexical.html.title: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Lexical | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Lexical.html.summary: Namespace ProvostXMemory.Lexical Classes Bm25Scorer BM25-lite scoring: saturated term frequency (k1 = 1.2) × IDF plus a key-match boost (default 2.0) on key-term hits and a modest single-term category match bonus (0.5). Classic BM25-lite: no length normalization, no third-party dependencies. Stateless pure scoring — corpus statistics are passed in per call (the index owns them). CorpusStatistics Immutable corpus-level statistics: document count plus per-term stats. LexicalDocument A tokenized document with optional key terms and category. LexicalIndex BM25-lite keyword index over documents. Inverted postings over body terms, plus key-term and exact-category maps so key-only and category-only matches surface. Scoring is delegated to IBm25Scorer; ordering is fully deterministic (score desc, then document id ascending). LexicalPosting One body posting: (document id, term frequency). LexicalTermCounts Term-frequency / token-set helpers over pre-tokenized term lists. Pure functions over their inputs; intentionally static per architecture rule. LexicalTokenizer Lowercases text and extracts contiguous [a0-9] word tokens (letters, digits, underscore). Pure helpers (stateless string transforms); intentionally static per architecture rule. ScoredLexicalId Lexical index search hit: id plus BM25-lite score. TermStat Immutable per-term corpus statistics for BM25 scoring. Interfaces IBm25Scorer BM25-lite scoring: saturated term frequency (k1 = 1.2) × IDF, plus a key-match boost on key-term hits and a single-term category match bonus. Corpus statistics are passed per call (owned by the index, which keeps them current after build/add). ILexicalIndex The lexical half of hybrid retrieval: a BM25-weighted inverted index over record text, kept in sync by the memory service (records remember/update → IncrementalAdd; forget → Remove). Complements the dense stage by matching exact terms embeddings miss (identifiers, acronyms, version numbers); both stages fuse into one ranking via IResultFuser. Contract: tokens are lowercase alphanumeric words (no stemming, no external NLP); scores are saturated-TF × IDF with a key-match boost. The index itself is not thread-safe — the memory service serializes all mutations; external callers must not share an instance unsynchronized.

api/ProvostXMemory.Reranking.IReranker.h.title: Interface IReranker | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Reranking.IReranker.h.summary: Interface IReranker The post-fusion scoring stage: reranks fused candidates against the query. The default ScoreBoostReranker adds deterministic boosts (tag/key/category term matches) and penalties (extremely short or long content) without ever dropping a candidate; a NoopReranker preserves fused order. Hosts may inject an LLM- or cross-encoder-backed reranker through this interface — the library stays model-free. Ranks exactly once: the retrieval pipeline reranks internally; a second pass over already-reranked results compounds boosts (found by audit) — hosts calling RerankAsync(RetrievalQuery, IReadOnlyList<ScoredMemoryRecord>, CancellationToken) directly own that responsibility. api/ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.QueryPlanRu.title: Class QueryPlanRunner | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.Retrieval.QueryPlanRu.summary: Class QueryPlanRunner Executes a declarative QueryPlan. Each step fans out to its target scopes (target scope strings are "<scope-kind>/<scope-id>" pairs; empty targets mean the query's own scope), runs the injected retriever in every target scope with per-scope ids namespaced, and merges the step lists via the injected IResultFuser. When every step's top score is below WeakEvidenceThreshold, a single second pass runs once against the rewritten text from the injected IQueryTextRewriter; its results replace the first pass. Record resolution happens against each target scope's own snapshot — a record id from scope A never resolves into scope B. api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.Hn.title: Class HnswBeamSearcher | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.Hn.summary: Class HnswBeamSearcher Exact analog of the canonical HNSW SEARCH-LAYER routine, in score form (higher = closer): candidate heap = max-heap by score (top = nearest candidate, expanded first), result heap = min-heap by score bounded to ef (top = worst kept result = the stop gate). A candidate whose score falls below the gate stops the beam. The visited set resets per layer traversal (canonical: fresh visited per searchLayer call); the query score cache lives in HnswSearchContext and persists across layers of the same query. Returns results sorted best-first (score desc, node id asc). api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.Hn.title: Class HnswIndex | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine.Hn.summary: Class HnswIndex Own-engine HNSW backend with IMMUTABLE-INDEX + BATCH-REBUILD semantics (patent-avoidance design, ARCHITECTURE.md addendum 2026-10-13): the layered graph is fully rebuilt from the item store on every Build, Add, and Remove — there is deliberately NO incremental update of a live graph, the method covered by US 15/929,802 "Dynamic Updates for HNSW". Same seed + same insertion order → same graph. HnswPublishedGraph The published immutable snapshot of a built HNSW graph: row-order ids parallel to the normalized vector rows and the graph topology. Swapped in atomically after each full rebuild; never mutated afterwards (batch-rebuild semantics). HnswSearchContext Reusable traversal context for one built HNSW graph: row-order ids parallel to normalized vector rows, a per-query dot-product score cache (NaN = unscored; zero-vector queries legitimately score 0 and MUST be rescored), and the visited set shared by construction-time multi-layer traversals. Score cache + visited set are reset per query (ResetForNewQuery()); the query is copied into a reusable buffer so no span state is held across calls. HnswSearcher Query-time traversal over a built HNSW graph: greedy descent from the entry point through upper layers to layer 1, then a single ef-bounded beam search on layer 0, sorted best-first. Read-only over the published immutable graph. IvfFlatIndex Own-engine IVF-Flat: deterministic k-means coarse quantizer + inverted lists; search probes the nprobe nearest clusters (by quantizer metric) and scores members exactly. Mutations mark the partition stale; the next search rebuilds it (batch-rebuild semantics per the 2026-10-13 addendum). Flush is a no-op (in-memory). IvfFlatIndex.Options Backend options: metric, cluster count, probe count, k-means effort, deterministic seed. Structs HnswCandidate A single candidate during graph traversal: node id + metric score.

api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.html.title: Namespace ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu.html.summary: Namespace ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu Classes DefaultGpuContextPolicy Default policy: GPU-first discovery (CUDA/OpenCL per options), optional CPU fallback acceptance (off by default — availability must reflect real GPUs only). Device selection prefers CUDA > OpenCL and never throws when none exist. GpuAccelerator Owns the ILGPU Context and the resolved accelerator. The GPU hand-shake runs once, lazily, on first access, inside a lock, and every failure mode (builder exception, missing driver, no acceptable device, accelerator-creation failure) collapses to IsAvailable=false. Nothing here throws for 'no GPU present'. GpuDiscoveryOptions How the ILGPU context is built for accelerator discovery. GPU-first builders enable CUDA/OpenCL discovery; the flag set mirrors what the host considers acceptable. GpuFlatIndex GPU-accelerated exact flat index (ILGPU kernel scan). When no GPU is available the injected CPU fallback IVectorIndex is used for every operation with identical semantics — the fallback path must pass the engine conformance suite unchanged. Kernels load lazily; all GPU faults collapse to CPU-fallback execution. GpuFlatIndex.Options Backend options: ranking metric (default cosine) + launch chunking. GpuIvfIndex GPU-accelerated IVF index: the deterministic engine k-means partitions the corpus (CPU-side, same algorithm as IvfFlatIndex so partitions are identical), GPU kernels score (1) coarse centroids and (2) in-cluster members. When no GPU is available the injected CPU fallback IVectorIndex is used with identical semantics. GpuIvfIndex.Options Backend options: mirrors the engine IVF options + ranking metric + launch chunking. GpuLaunchOptions Kernel-launch policy: rows per launch chunk and the per-launch thread cap. Chunked launches keep the per-thread flat loop short and bounded on every backend (including ILGPU's CPU simulator, which materializes one thread per index). GpuMetricCodec Mapping from the engine metric enum onto the GPU kernel's int metric code. GpuVectorIndexFactory Factory that produces GpuFlatIndex for Gpu and delegates every other kind to the injected CPU IVectorIndexFactory. The GPU index receives the standard IGpuAccelerator availability gate and wraps a flat CPU fallback IVectorIndex as its transparent CPU fallback, so search semantics are identical whether or not an accelerator is present. GpuVectorKernels ILGPU kernels: one thread per score slot, plain loops, no barriers/shared memory — identical accumulation order on every backend (CPU simulator included), so GPU and fallback results are bit-for-bit reproducible for the same inputs. GpuVectorMatrix GPU-resident row-major vector matrix with lazy (re)upload: CPU-side rows + norms are mirrored to device buffers; uploads overwrite exactly the changed range. Ownership and synchronization live here — indexes never touch ILGPU buffers directly. IlgpuScoreLauncher Lazy, guarded ILGPU kernel launcher: kernels compile on first launch only (never at construction), launches are chunked per GpuLaunchOptions, and every launch ends with a synchronize so scored results are deterministically visible on the host. Interfaces IGpuAccelerator Availability handle for the ILGPU runtime: owns the Context and exposes the resolved accelerator lazily. Construction never throws and never touches GPU drivers; every member is guarded so machines without CUDA/OpenCL observe IsAvailable=false. IGpuContextPolicy ILGPU accelerator hand-shake: a GPU-first context (CUDA + OpenCL as configured) with device classes the caller considers acceptable. All discovery is exception- guarded; a machine without GPU drivers simply observes IsAvailable=false. IGpuScoreLauncher Compiled-kernel launcher boundary: hides ILGPU's launcher delegates behind an injectable abstraction so index classes stay backend-agnostic and testable. Enums GpuDistanceMetric Backend metric shared with the engine kernels (mirrors VectorDistanceMetric).

api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorEm.summary: Interface IVectorEmbedder The host-injected embedding seam. The library never bundles, downloads, or selects embedding models — it consumes vectors from whatever IVectorEmbedder the host wires in, and it validates them instead: ModelHash and Dim are recorded with every vector namespace, and any index whose hash or dimension mismatches the embedder is rejected rather than silently mixing embeddings from different models. Zero-norm vectors (all-zero) are tolerated — retrieval falls back to lexical scoring for degenerate cases. Typical wiring: an ONNX runtime embedding model (the ProvostX Inference satellite provides one), any remote embedding API, or a deterministic fake in tests. api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorIn.title: Interface IVectorIndex | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.IVectorIn.summary: Interface IVectorIndex The pluggable dense-vector index contract. The library ships four backends, all interchangeable through this interface (they pass one shared conformance suite): IndexKind.FlatJson (zero-dependency JSON file, brute-force cosine), IndexKind.Flat (in-memory exact search with SIMD kernels), IndexKind.Ivf (k-means inverted lists for corpus sizes where full scans get expensive), and IndexKind.Hnsw (navigable-small-world graph; built with immutable/rebuild semantics and searched with a layered greedy beam). A GPU tier (ILGPU, transparent CPU fallback) wraps any of these for machines with devices. Vector contract: vectors are L2-normalized at index time; scores are cosine similarities (higher = closer, 1.0 = identical). Dim is fixed at construction; every item/query with a different dimension is rejected. Concurrency: implementations own their internal synchronization; concurrent Add/Remove/Search from multiple threads is safe. Backends compare sets, not orderings: ranking parity between backends is exact for Flat/FlatJson and statistically guaranteed (recall ≥0.95 on the fixture) for the ANN tiers — results are ranked identically after fusion because ordering derives from scores, not insertion sequence. api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.html.title: Namespace ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.html.summary: Namespace ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex Classes FlatJsonVectorIndex Default zero-dependency backend over the JSON namespace-file format: brute-force cosine (dot product over L2-normalized vectors), transactional flush. IvfMember One IVF member: id, vector, assigned cluster. IvfPostingLists Inverted lists: cluster id → member rows + centroid access for probing. KMeansQuantizer OWN deterministic k-means (Lloyd iterations, seeded) — the IVF coarse quantizer. Deterministic given the same training rows: seeded Fisher-Yates seeding, squared-L2 assignment via the SIMD scanner, mean update, empty clusters reseated on the globally farthest points (deterministic order). Internally uses squared L2 regardless of the search metric — IVF coarse assignment is metric-agnostic partitioning. KMeansResult Result of one k-means run: centroids plus label arrays over the training rows. ScalarVectorOps In-package scalar math for the FlatJson backend (instance-based, no static state). Deliberately separate from the Engine package's SIMD VectorMath: the base package must stay dependency-free below itself, and cosine/normalize here are O(dim) scalar loops — the flat JSON backend's cost is dominated by I/O, not arithmetic. ScoredVectorId Vector index search hit. SeededRandom Pure deterministic pseudo-random generator (xorshift64*) used wherever the engine needs seeded randomness (level assignment, quantizer seeding). Own implementation instead of Random so results are stable across .NET versions and platforms. Thread-unsafe by design: engine components own dedicated instances. VectorIndexGuard Guard record binding a vector namespace to an embedder model hash/dim. VectorIndexGuardMismatchException Embedder model hash or vector dimension does not match the index guard. VectorIndexIdNotFoundException Remove of an id that is not present in the index. VectorItem A vector index item: id + vector. VectorItemStore Mutable in-memory store shared by engine indexes: ids in row order parallel to vector rows plus id → row map. Owns synchronization; build/add/remove/dim-guard semantics. VectorMath PURE STATIC UTILITY (no mutable state, thread-safe by construction; the one sanctioned static exception per architecture principles). Stateless numeric kernels for the engine: dot product via Vector512 → Vector256 → Vector128 with scalar fallback, norm, normalize, cosine. Deterministic order of accumulation for a given hardware width. VectorNamespaceFile On-disk JSON vector index file format (one file per scope/model-hash namespace): temp-file + atomic swap on write; open enforces the model-hash/dim guard. VectorNamespaceFile.Content Content of one namespace file: guard + entries. VectorNamespaceFile.Entry Sets are keyed by id; a re-set id replaces the entry. VectorScanner Scans rows with the metric's SIMD kernel; shared scoring core for flat/IVF search. VectorTopKBuffer Bounded top-k min-heap buffer over (id, score); scores rise to the top. Interfaces IVectorEmbedder The host-injected embedding seam. The library never bundles, downloads, or selects embedding models — it consumes vectors from whatever IVectorEmbedder the host wires in, and it validates them instead: ModelHash and Dim are recorded with every vector namespace, and any index whose hash or dimension mismatches the embedder is rejected rather than silently mixing embeddings from different models. IVectorIndex The pluggable dense-vector index contract. The library ships four backends, all interchangeable through this interface (they pass one shared conformance suite): IndexKind.FlatJson (zero-dependency JSON file, brute-force cosine), IndexKind.Flat (in-memory exact search with SIMD kernels), IndexKind.Ivf (k-means inverted lists for corpus sizes where full scans get expensive), and IndexKind.Hnsw (navigable-small-world graph; built with immutable/rebuild semantics and searched with a layered greedy beam). A GPU tier (ILGPU, transparent CPU fallback) wraps any of these for machines with devices. Vector contract: vectors are L2-normalized at index time; scores are cosine similarities (higher = closer, 1.0 = identical). Dim is fixed at construction; every item/query with a different dimension is rejected. Concurrency: implementations own their internal synchronization; concurrent Add/Remove/Search from multiple threads is safe. Backends compare sets, not orderings: ranking parity between backends is exact for Flat/FlatJson and statistically guaranteed (recall ≥0.95 on the fixture) for the ANN tiers — results are ranked identically after fusion because ordering derives from scores, not insertion sequence. IVectorIndexFactory Creates vector indexes of a requested IndexKind for one dimension. Implementations decide concrete wiring (metrics, seeds, backing storage); the factory keeps index creation out of retrieval code so backends stay swappable by configuration alone. The default EngineVectorIndexFactory produces the own-engine backends; the GPU factory decorates a CPU fallback with ILGPU kernels. IVectorIndexGuard Guards model hash + vector dimension at every index mutation boundary. Enums VectorDistanceMetric Distance metric for vector-to-vector comparisons inside the engine.

api/ProvostXMemory.html.title: Namespace ProvostXMemory | ProvostXMemory API
api/ProvostXMemory.html.summary: Namespace ProvostXMemory Classes DefaultEvalServiceFactory Default eval wiring: a real MemoryService over the transactional JSONL store + own-engine flat index + RRF, powered by the deterministic ClusterHashEmbedder (no real model anywhere). Any host can substitute its own EvalServiceFactory to eval its production wiring instead. EvalRunner Runs an EvalCaseSet against a freshly built service from an EvalServiceFactory: materializes the corpus records under a fresh temp root, builds indexes per scope, replays every golden query, computes all metrics and breakdowns, checks thresholds, and produces a JSON-serializable EvalReport. The runner never constructs a service itself — hosts control wiring via the factory. EvalRunnerOptions Per-run knobs for EvalRunner. GraphIndexLedger Index-time graph maintenance over the scope-pinned IMemoryGraphStore (resolved via IMemoryGraphStoreResolver): per record, the wired IEntityExtractor's entities/relations are upserted for the record's scope only; when a record is forgotten, its mentions are dropped by re-extracting the scope's remaining snapshot. The ledger itself holds no per-record entity cache — graph stores accumulate weight by design, so Forget rebuilds the affected entity mention lists from the surviving records. Scope comes from the record; the resolver is scope-exact by contract. MemoryService Composition root: takes MemoryServiceOptions plus injected dependencies and owns the configured retrieval pipeline. Remember/Forget/Update maintain the per-scope indexes alongside the store; Recall routes through hybrid → optional corrective → plan (when the query carries one) → optional rerank. Every store access goes through the scope-bound IMemoryStore API, so cross-scope isolation is structural. Per-scope indexes are created lazily and registered scope-exact. MemoryServiceBuilder Fluent wiring helper for MemoryService. Collects the host's choices and hands them to the MemoryService constructor — still plain constructor injection underneath, no service locator, no ambient container. MemoryServicePipelineOptions Pipeline wiring knobs layered over MemoryServiceOptions: which extra retrieval stages run during Recall/Remember and maintenance bounds for index updates. RootChildScopeResolver Default plan-fan-out scope resolution: a target string names either the root scope itself ("<Kind>/<Id>", case-insensitive) or a child scope built via WithParent(MemoryScope) ("<ChildKind>/<ChildId>" over the root). Resolving a child pins the parent, so fan-out targets are always descendants or the root itself — never unrelated scopes. Interfaces EvalServiceFactory Host-pluggable service construction for eval runs: given a fresh root path the host builds an IMemoryService exactly as it does in production. Implementations must return a service with no records yet — the runner owns corpus loadout and index building. IMemoryService The single public surface of the ProvostXMemory library. Host applications see this interface — plus the options records they pass to MemoryServiceBuilder — and nothing else. Every capability of the library (durable storage, hybrid lexical and dense-vector retrieval, fusion, reranking, optional corrective and graph retrieval, consolidation, and audit-grade logging) is reachable through the members below. Scope isolation. Every record belongs to exactly one MemoryScope (platform, session, tenant, purpose, or custom). Every operation is scope-bound; a record written to scope A is structurally invisible to operations on scope B — the storage layout and the index registry make cross-scope access impossible rather than merely discouraged. Concurrency. Implementations are safe for concurrent use from multiple threads. Mutations (Remember/Update/Forget) are serialized per service instance; embedding computation happens outside the serialization gate, so concurrent callers do not block on model latency. IScopesAware Implemented by stores that can enumerate their scopes natively.
