docs/api-glossary.html.title: API Glossary | ProvostXMemory API
docs/api-glossary.html.summary: API Glossary Reference for the public types of ProvostXMemory, grouped by namespace. Hosts normally interact only with the root facade, the abstractions, and the backend factories; the remaining namespaces document the contracts behind each capability. Legend: interfaces are marked I, classes C, records R, enums E. ProvostXMemory (facade) IMemoryService (I) The single public surface of the library. Every operation is scope-bound. Member Description RememberAsync(record, ct?) Stores a record and maintains dense/lexical indexes (and the optional graph ledger). ForgetAsync(scope, id, ct?) Deletes a record and its index artifacts in that scope. GetAsync(scope, id, ct?) Returns the record or null; scope-exact. UpdateAsync(record, ct?) Updates record content/metadata and refreshes index entries. RecallAsync(query, ct?) Runs the retrieval pipeline; routes plan → corrective → hybrid, then optional rerank. ConsolidateAsync(scope, options, ct?) Runs a consolidation pass and refreshes index artifacts. BuildIndexesAsync(scope, ct?) Chunks, embeds, and builds vector + lexical indexes for a scope. RebuildAsync(ct?) Rebuilds indexes for all known scopes (deterministic; identical rankings). Scopes() Enumerates scopes known under the root. Usage note: this is the only type most hosts need beyond options and factories. See Getting Started. MemoryService (C) Composition root implementing IMemoryService. Constructor takes MemoryServiceOptions plus injected dependencies: store, embedder, index factory, fuser, telemetry, and optional grader, graph extractor, reranker, chunker (+ ChunkOptions), pipeline options, graph-store resolver, and log sink. Not typically constructed directly — use the builder. MemoryServiceBuilder (C) Fluent wiring helper; plain constructor injection underneath (no service locator). Member Description WithOptions(options) Root options (required). WithStore(store) IMemoryStore implementation (required). WithEmbedder(embedder) Host embedding model (required). WithIndexFactory(factory) Backend factory (required). WithFuser(fuser) Result fuser (required). WithTelemetry(telemetry) Telemetry sink (required; NoopMemoryTelemetry.Instance for silence). WithGrader(grader) Optional; enables the corrective recall route. WithGraphExtractor(...) / graph-store resolver Optional graph ingestion. WithReranker(reranker) Optional post-fusion reranking. WithChunker(chunker, options) Optional custom chunking. WithLogSink(sink) Optional injected log sink. Build() Validates all required wiring and returns IMemoryService. IScopesAware (I) Optional store hook: Scopes() returns all scopes currently known to the store. Enables IMemoryService.Scopes(); the facade falls back to the directory layout when the store does not implement it. GraphIndexLedger (C) Keeps the scope's graph store in sync with record mutations (entity upsert/removal driven by the injected IEntityExtractor, including consolidation cluster writes). ProvostXMemory.Abstractions Core contracts and immutable data types shared by every layer. MemoryRecord (R) Immutable memory unit. Members: Id, Scope, Key, Content, Category?, Tags, Reps, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, ExpiresAt?, Meta. See Concepts. MemoryScope (R) and MemoryScopeKind (E) Hierarchical isolation boundary: (Kind, Id, ParentScope?) with kinds Platform | Session | Tenant | Purpose | Custom. Members: PathSegment, Chain(), Contains(other), WithParent(parent). See Scopes. MemoryRepresentation (R), MemoryRepresentationModality (E) One modality-specific representation of a record: Modality (Text | Image | Table | Audio | Custom), Content, optional EmbeddingModelHash, Properties metadata. RetrievalQuery (R) Text, Scope, TopK (default set by VectorOptions.DefaultTopK), Filters?, Plan?. RetrievalFilters (R) Tags, Category?, From?, To? — enforced after candidate resolution. RetrievalResult (R) Records (IReadOnlyList<ScoredMemoryRecord>) and Diagnostics (IReadOnlyList<RetrievalStageDiagnostics>: stage name, duration, per-stage scores). ScoredMemoryRecord (R) Record, Score, Provenance (RetrievalProvenance: retriever name + stage scores). QueryPlan (R), QueryPlanStep (R) Declarative retrieval plan: PlanId + ordered steps; each step has StepId, Action, TargetScopes, TopK. IMemoryStore (I) Scope-bound CRUD over records. Member Description AddAsync / UpdateAsync Persist a record in its scope. DeleteAsync(scopeKind, scopeId, id) Remove one record. GetAsync(scopeKind, scopeId, id) Scope-exact fetch; null when absent. ListAsync(scopeKind, scopeId) All records of the scope. CountAsync(scopeKind, scopeId) Record count. SnapshotAsync(scopeKind, scopeId) Consistent snapshot for index builds. Usage note: hosts rarely implement this; use JsonlMemoryStore. Custom implementations must remain scope-exact. IJsonlMemoryStore (I) Contract marker for the default JSONL store implementation (ProvostXMemory.Storage). IMemoryManifestCodec (I) Reads/writes the root manifest.json (MemoryManifest: schema id, counts, timestamps; row model MemoryEntryModel persists records with backward-compatible Reps/Meta). Options records Type Members (defaults) MemoryServiceOptions (R) Storage, Vector, Graph, Fusion, Consolidation, optional Logging. StorageOptions (R) Root, AtomicWrites = true, Fsync. VectorOptions (R) ModelHash, Dim, IndexKind = Flat, DefaultTopK. GraphOptions (R) Enabled = true, MaxNeighbors = 16, MaxHops = 2, MaxClusters = 5; GraphOptions.Default. FusionOptions (R) RrfK = 60, DenseWeight, LexicalWeight. ConsolidationOptions (R) DedupSimilarityThreshold, ExpireTtl, EmitClusterSummaries. ChunkOptions (R) MaxChunkLength = 512, Overlap, RespectStructure, Separator?, MinChunkLength. Supporting types BackendStats (R) — item count, dimension stats, LastFlushedAt; ScoredId (R) — scope-qualified id + score used by fusion; QueryTokens (C) — query tokenization helper. ProvostXMemory.Storage MemoryRootLayout (C) Resolves root + scope paths (root/scopeKind/scopeId/modelHash); the structural basis of scope isolation. Constructor takes the root path and the model hash. JsonlMemoryStore (C) : IJsonlMemoryStore Default store: one JSONL file per scope (records.jsonl), transactional writes. AtomicFileWriter (C) Temp-file + atomic-swap writer with optional fsync; all durable file writes flow through it. MemoryManifestCodec (C) : IMemoryManifestCodec Manifest (de)serialization. ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex IVectorIndex (I) Member Description Dim, Count Dimension and item count. BuildAsync(items) Replace contents with the given VectorItem set. AddAsync(item) / RemoveAsync(id) Incremental mutation. SearchAsync(vector, k) Top-k search → ScoredVectorId list. FlushAsync Persist durable state. Usage note: all backends implement this and pass the same conformance suite. IVectorIndexFactory (I) Create(kind, dim) returns an index of IndexKind (Flat | Ivf | Hnsw | Gpu). IVectorEmbedder (I) Host-injected embedder: ModelHash, Dim, EmbedAsync(text). The library validates hash/dimension but never chooses models. IVectorIndexGuard (I) Model-hash/dimension guard consulted when opening persisted index artifacts. VectorNamespaceFile (C) Per-scope/model-hash index file format (FlatJson backend persistence). Exceptions VectorIndexGuardMismatchException — model hash or dimension mismatch on open. VectorIndexIdNotFoundException — unknown vector id requested for removal/resolution. Supporting types VectorItem (R) — id + vector; ScoredVectorId (R) — id + score; ScalarVectorOps (C) — scalar distance helpers. ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine Own C# vector engine; zero third-party vector dependencies (ILGPU — the GPU compiler for the included kernels, NCSA license — is the sole non-vector dependency and falls back to the CPU bit-identically). Namespace name reflects history; the FAISS dependency was replaced by this engine. EngineVectorIndexFactory (C) : IVectorIndexFactory Creates FlatExactIndex, IvfFlatIndex, or HnswIndex; rejects IndexKind.Gpu (explicit GPU routing only). FlatExactIndex (C) : IVectorIndex Exact brute-force search with SIMD (Vector512) kernels. IvfFlatIndex (C) : IVectorIndex k-means coarse quantizer + inverted posting lists; nprobe-style partial scan. Supporting: KMeansQuantizer, KMeansResult, IvfPostingLists, IvfMember. HnswIndex (C) : IVectorIndex Hierarchical navigable small-world graph. Immutable after build; mutations trigger batch rebuild (patent-safe semantics). Supporting: HnswBuilder, HnswGraph, HnswSearcher, HnswBeamSearcher, HnswSearchContext, HnswLevelAssigner, HnswPublishedGraph, HnswOptions (seeded, deterministic builds). Options (C) — engine options Three overloads configure the metric (flat/IVF), full HNSW parameters (connectivity, ef-construction/ef-search, levels, seed), and composition of engine-level options. Supporting types VectorMath, VectorScanner, VectorTopKBuffer (SIMD kernels and top-k buffering); VectorItemStore (id → vector storage); SeededRandom (deterministic randomness). ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu ILGPU-backed GPU kernels with transparent CPU fallback. IGpuAccelerator (I) / GpuAccelerator (C) Lazy, exception-guarded accelerator discovery and kernel launches; IDisposable. IGpuContextPolicy (I) / DefaultGpuContextPolicy (C) Controls accelerator context creation (including a force-CPU test mode). IGpuScoreLauncher (I) / IlgpuScoreLauncher (C) Launches similarity kernels over a GpuVectorMatrix batch; GpuLaunchOptions (chunk size, max parallel batches). GpuFlatIndex (C), GpuIvfIndex (C) : IVectorIndex GPU versions of flat exact and IVF search. Delegate to an injected CPU IVectorIndex when no accelerator is available — bit-identical results by construction (no barriers/shared memory; one thread per slot, chunked launches). GpuVectorIndexFactory (C) : IVectorIndexFactory Composes GPU indexes with an EngineVectorIndexFactory fallback. Supporting types GpuDiscoveryOptions, GpuLaunchOptions, GpuVectorKernels, GpuVectorMatrix, GpuMetricCodec; per-backend Options records. ProvostXMemory.Lexical ILexicalIndex (I) Member Description Count, Statistics Document count; live corpus statistics. Build(documents) Replace contents. IncrementalAdd(document) Add one document (duplicate ids throw). Remove(documentId) Remove by id; false when unknown. EnumerateDocuments() Deterministic id-ordered snapshot. Search(queryTokens, topK) BM25-scored top-k → ScoredLexicalId. Usage note: documents are pre-tokenized (LexicalDocument: Id, BodyTerms, KeyTerms?, Category?); tokenization itself is LexicalTokenizer. IBm25Scorer (I) / Bm25Scorer (C) Saturated-TF IDF scoring (k1 = 1.2) with key-term boost (default 2.0) and a category-match bonus. Corpus statistics are passed per call. Supporting types LexicalPosting (R) — (document id, term frequency); LexicalTermCounts, TermStat (R) — corpus statistics primitives. ProvostXMemory.Fusion IResultFuser (I) / ReciprocalRankFuser (C) Fuses multiple ranked lists into one. Default implementation: Reciprocal Rank Fusion with FusionOptions.RrfK (default 60) and configurable dense/lexical weights; zero weights drop a stage; deterministic tie ordering. Fusion ids are scope-qualified so identical record ids across scopes never conflate. ProvostXMemory.Chunking IChunker (I) Split(record, options) → Chunk[]. Implementations: StructuredChunker (structure-respecting), SizeChunker (size/overlap). IParentResolver (I) / ChunkParentResolver (C) Chunk id → parent record lookup for parent-document recall. ChunkIdCodec (C), ChunkIdParts (R) Encode/decode scope-qualified chunk ids (scope kind, scope id, record id, chunk index). ProvostXMemory.Reranking IReranker (I) Rerank(query, candidates) → re-ranked candidates. Implementations: Type Behavior NoopReranker Pass-through. ScoreBoostReranker Heuristic boosts (tag/key/category) + length penalties via ScoreBoostRerankerOptions. ClientBackedReranker Delegates to IRerankerClient with fallback fusion; ClientBackedRerankerOptions.TrustClientCompletely. IRerankerClient (I) Optional external rerank service contract (host-implemented; typically calls a cross-encoder or LLM endpoint). ProvostXMemory.Correction IRetrievalGrader (I) GradeAsync(query, candidate) → GradedCandidate (RetrievalGrade: Relevant | Irrelevant | Uncertain). Host-injected. IQueryRewriter (I) / KeywordQueryRewriter (C) Query rewriting for the corrective retry. IExternalFetcher (I) Extension hook invoked when retrieval returns empty and CorrectionOptions.UseFetcherOnEmpty is set (e.g. web augmentation). The library never fetches on its own. CorrectiveRetriever (C) : ICorrectiveRetriever Orchestrates grade → rewrite → retry loop; CorrectionOptions (RelevanceFloor, UseFetcherOnEmpty). Supporting types StageNames (C) — stable stage-name constants for diagnostics. ProvostXMemory.Graph IMemoryGraphStore (I) Member Description UpsertEntityAsync / UpsertRelationAsync Insert or update graph nodes/edges. UpsertClusterAsync(cluster) Replace-by-id cluster write (authoritative, not accumulating). GetEntityAsync(id) Fetch entity or null. SearchEntitiesAsync(query, max) Whole-token name/alias match, strongest overlap first. RelationsOfAsync(id, max) Undirected relations, strongest support first. NeighborsAsync(id, max) Direct neighbors. ShortestPathAsync(from, to) Shortest entity path. ClusterOfAsync(id) Cluster containing the entity, if any. Default implementation: JsonlMemoryGraphStore (scope-pinned JSONL files). IMemoryGraphStoreResolver supplies per-scope stores. IEntityExtractor (I) / HeuristicEntityExtractor (C) Extracts entities + relations from records (ExtractionResult). Hosts may inject an LLM-backed extractor. IGraphRetriever (I) / GraphRetriever (C) Retrieves records from the query-relevant subgraph plus cluster summaries; tuned by GraphOptions. Data records GraphEntity (R) — id, name, aliases, record links; GraphRelation (R) — source, target, type, support; GraphCluster (R) — id, members, summary record id. ProvostXMemory.Consolidation IMemoryConsolidator (I) ConsolidateAsync(scopeKind, scopeId, options) → surviving records. Default: MemoryConsolidator. IDedupDetector (I) / ThresholdDedupDetector (C) Near-duplicate detection by embedding similarity threshold. IClusterSummarizer (I) / ClusterSummarizer (C) Produces a summary record for a cluster; tuned by ConsolidationTuning. Supporting types ConsolidationReportMeta (C) — pass report metadata. ProvostXMemory.Retrieval IHybridRetriever (I) / HybridRetriever (C) Dense + lexical in parallel → fuse → resolve → optional rerank. Constructor takes the scope index registry, embedder, fuser, and optional telemetry, reranker, FusionOptions. IScopeIndexRegistry (I) / InMemoryScopeIndexRegistry (C) Maps a scope to its artifacts: GetVectorIndex(scope), GetLexicalIndex(scope), GetRecordProvider(scope), HasIndexes(scope). Implementations must be scope-exact — no parent fallthrough, no default forwarding. The in-memory registry keys on the exact (Kind, Id) pair and also exposes Register* methods and a Reset. ICorrectiveRetriever (I) Corrective-loop retrieval contract (implemented by CorrectiveRetriever). IGraphRetrieverImpl (I) Graph retrieval implementation contract (implemented by GraphRetriever). IMultiRepresentationRetriever (I) / MultiRepresentationRetriever (C) Query across modalities; resolves repr|<recordId>|<index> ids to best-representation scores per record. IQueryPlanRunner (I) / QueryPlanRunner (C) Executes QueryPlans: scope fan-out, merge, one weak-evidence rewrite retry (IQueryTextRewriter, default KeywordQueryTextRewriter; QueryPlanRunnerOptions). IScopeResolver (I) / RootChildScopeResolver (C) Resolves plan target scope ids to concrete scopes (root + child interpretation). RetrievalFilterApplier (C) Enforces RetrievalFilters on resolved candidates. ProvostXMemory.Eval EvalServiceFactory (I) / DefaultEvalServiceFactory (C) Create(rootPath) builds a self-contained IMemoryService for evaluation; default factory composes the standard stack at a given vector dimension. EvalRunner (C) Member Description LoadAsync(corpus, rootPath) Materializes the corpus into a fresh service and builds indexes. RunAsync(corpus, caseSet, options?) Full run on a fresh temp root: load → index → evaluate → report (root deleted unless EvalRunnerOptions.DisposeRootDirectory = false). EvaluateAsync(service, caseSet, options, totalRecords) Evaluates an already-loaded service. EvalCase (C), EvalCaseSet (C) Golden case: Id, Query, QueryScope, RelevantIds, optional graded relevance (0..1 per id; binary 1.0 when absent); RelevanceOf(recordId). EvalCaseSet is a named, ordered case collection. EvalRunnerOptions (C), EvalMetricThresholds (C) TopK, Thresholds (per-metric floors: recallAtK, precisionAtK, mrr, ndcgAtK), DisposeRootDirectory. Results EvalCaseMetrics (R) — per-case metrics; EvalMetricBreakdownEntry (R) — per-scope/per-stage breakdowns; EvalCaseTrace/EvalCaseTraceHit (R) — hit traces with gains; MetricThresholdViolation (R) — metric, actual, threshold; MetricThresholdViolations (C) — violation collection; EvalReportJson (C) — canonical snake_case JSON codec. Deterministic corpus DeterministicEvalCorpus (C) — seeded synthetic corpus (records, clusters, vector dimension); ClusterHashEmbedder (C) — deterministic embedder for reproducible runs; EvalMetricMath (C) — the metric implementations; MemoryScopeComparer (C) — deterministic scope ordering. ProvostXMemory.Logging MemoryLoggingOptions (R) Enabled, Level, Sink, Directory, FileNamePattern, Format, IncludeContent, Integrity, RetentionDays — see the options table. MemoryLogLevel (E), MemoryLogSinkKind (E), MemoryLogFormat (E), MemoryLogIntegrity (E) Level (Debug/Info/Warn/Error); sink (File/Console/Injected); format (JSON Lines); integrity (hash-chain toggle). IMemoryLogSink (I) WriteAsync(entry) — destination for MemoryLogEntry. Built-in: FileMemoryLogSink (rolling), ConsoleMemoryLogSink. MemoryLogger (C) Central emitter; applies level filtering, format encoding, and chain appending. Disabled = zero writes/allocations. MemoryLogEntry (R), MemoryLogScope (R) Entry payload: timestamp, sequence, level, category, scope, correlation id, duration, chain hashes, optional content excerpt. HashChainAppender (C), LogChainVerifier (C), LogChainVerificationResult (R) SHA-256 chain append and verification (IsValid, broken-at sequence, detail). RetentionSweeper (C) Deletes log files older than RetentionDays; explicit scheduling. ProvostXMemory.Telemetry IMemoryTelemetry (I) Query timings, per-stage scores, backend stats — host-injected sink. Implementation Behavior NoopMemoryTelemetry Silence (default; Instance). InMemoryMemoryTelemetry Collects events in memory for tests/diagnostics.

docs/backends.html.title: Backends | ProvostXMemory API
docs/backends.html.summary: Backends Every vector index backend implements the same IVectorIndex contract and must pass the same conformance suite (build, add, remove, search, flush, dimension/count invariants). Switching backends is a configuration change: set VectorOptions.IndexKind and wire the matching IVectorIndexFactory. The contract Member Description Build(items) Replaces index contents with the given VectorItem set. Add(item) / Remove(id) Incremental mutation (where supported). Search(vector, k) Returns ScoredVectorId list, best first. Dim / Count Dimension and current item count. Flush Persists durable state. Guards (IVectorIndexGuard) protect against dimension and model-hash mismatches; violations throw VectorIndexGuardMismatchException. Missing ids throw VectorIndexIdNotFoundException. FlatJson (default, core package) Mechanism: vectors held in a per-scope VectorNamespaceFile (transactional JSON file, written via AtomicFileWriter); search is brute-force cosine over the scope's items. Complexity: build O(n·d); search O(n·d) per query. When to choose: small scopes (up to a few thousand vectors), persistence-first deployments, environments where zero extra dependencies matter. It is also the parity baseline all other backends are tested against. Persistence: JSON in the scope's vectors/<model-hash>/ directory; survives restarts without a rebuild. FlatExact (own engine, SIMD) Package: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine. Mechanism: exact brute-force search with Vector512 SIMD kernels (VectorMath, VectorScanner, VectorTopKBuffer); in-memory item store with configurable distance metric (Engine Options). Complexity: build O(n·d); search O(n·d) but with a large SIMD constant-factor win over FlatJson. When to choose: exactness required and up to ~10k vectors per scope; also the reference result source for cross-backend parity tests. IVF (own engine) Package: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine. Mechanism: k-means coarse quantizer (KMeansQuantizer, seeded and deterministic) partitions vectors into inverted posting lists; a query scans only the nearest nprobe lists. IvfPostingLists, IvfMember, KMeansResult are the supporting types. Complexity: build O(iterations · n · d); search O(nprobe/ncentroids · n · d) — sublinear in n. Trade-off: recall depends on nprobe; results are deterministic for a given seed and build order. When to choose: 10k–1M vectors where a small, tunable recall loss buys large search-speed gains. HNSW (own engine) Package: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine. Mechanism: hierarchical navigable small-world graph — HnswBuilder constructs layered graphs (HnswGraph), level assignment is seeded (HnswLevelAssigner), search is greedy beam descent (HnswSearcher, HnswBeamSearcher). Complexity: build O(n·log n·d); search approximately O(log n·d). Patent-safe semantics: indexes are immutable after build; mutations trigger a batch rebuild. This deliberately avoids incremental dynamic-update methods (see the patent addendum in ARCHITECTURE.md). Quality: measured recall@10 = 0.998 on a 2000×64 synthetic corpus; two identical builds produce bit-identical results (determinism pinned by tests). When to choose: 10k–10M vectors with high recall requirements and read-mostly workloads. GPU (ILGPU) Package: ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu. Mechanism: own ILGPU kernels for exact flat scoring and IVF list scans (GpuVectorKernels, IlgpuScoreLauncher, GpuVectorMatrix). Kernels are one-thread-per-slot with chunked launches — no barriers or shared memory — so accumulation order is identical to CPU: results are bit-exact between GPU and fallback paths. Availability: IGpuAccelerator discovery is lazy and exception-guarded (IGpuContextPolicy, GpuDiscoveryOptions). On machines without a compatible accelerator the index transparently delegates to an injected CPU IVectorIndex with identical results; the same conformance suite passes on CPU-only machines via this path. Factories: GpuVectorIndexFactory wraps an EngineVectorIndexFactory for the fallback; the engine factory itself rejects IndexKind.Gpu by design (explicit routing, pinned by tests). When to choose: Flat/IVF-sized workloads where an accelerator is present and batch scoring throughput matters. Selection matrix Backend Exact? Scale guidance Extra package Native deps FlatJson yes ≤ a few thousand per scope none none FlatExact yes ≤ ~10k per scope Engine none IVF approximate (tunable) 10k–1M Engine none HNSW approximate 10k–10M Engine none GPU (Flat/IVF) exact (bit-identical) Flat/IVF scale, accelerator-dependent Gpu GPU runtime via ILGPU Rules of thumb: start with FlatJson; move to HNSW when a scope outgrows brute-force latency; use IVF when you can trade a little recall for speed; configure GPU unconditionally when hardware may be present — the fallback makes it safe to configure unconditionally.

docs/concepts.html.title: Concepts | ProvostXMemory API
docs/concepts.html.summary: Concepts The memory model of ProvostXMemory: what a record is, how scopes isolate data, how representations and chunking work, and how the model-hash guard protects index consistency. Records A MemoryRecord is the atomic unit of memory. It is an immutable record type: Member Description Id Stable identifier; unique within its scope. Scope The MemoryScope this record belongs to (isolation boundary). Key Short symbolic name (also boosted in lexical scoring). Content Primary text content. Category Optional single-value classification, filterable. Tags Optional label set, filterable; stored normalized (empty list, never null). Reps Additional MemoryRepresentation entries (multi-modal). CreatedAt / UpdatedAt UTC timestamps, set on creation and maintained by the facade. ExpiresAt Optional TTL deadline; honored by consolidation. Meta Free-form string key/value metadata, persisted with the record. Hosts create records; the facade owns index maintenance. RememberAsync, UpdateAsync, and ForgetAsync keep the dense and lexical indexes (and optionally the graph ledger) in sync through a per-record id ledger. Scopes and the isolation model A MemoryScope is (Kind, Id, ParentScope?) — hierarchical and immutable: Kinds: Platform, Session, Tenant, Purpose, Custom. Chain() flattens the parent chain, outermost first. Contains(other) reports whether other is this scope or a descendant. Isolation is structural, not conventional: every store, index, and graph operation is scope-bound, and scope resolution is enforced by MemoryRootLayout, which maps each scope to its own directory subtree. Cross-scope reads are impossible by construction — a query in scope A cannot observe records, vectors, or graph entities of scope B. This property is pinned by dedicated isolation tests in every layer and by end-to-end multi-tenant journey tests. Parent chains are host-side metadata: they express intent (a session belonging to a tenant) and participate in Contains semantics, but persistence equality is by kind + id — scopes are stored under their own resolved paths regardless of parentage. Representations One record can carry multiple MemoryRepresentation entries with modality Text | Image | Table | Audio | Custom and an optional per-representation EmbeddingModelHash. This supports multi-modal memory: a table and its textual description can live on the same record and be embedded separately. Retrieval addresses representations with vector ids of the form repr|<recordId>|<index>. The multi-representation retriever resolves these back to the owning record and reports the best-representation score per record, so one hit per record per stage regardless of how many representations matched. Chunking Long content is split into Chunk items before embedding. IChunker implementations: StructuredChunker — respects document structure (line/paragraph boundaries) when ChunkOptions.RespectStructure is set. SizeChunker — size/overlap-driven splitting. ChunkOptions controls MaxChunkLength (default 512), Overlap, MinChunkLength, Separator, and structure respect; all combinations are validated (overlap must be smaller than the max length, minimum must not exceed the maximum, and so on). Chunk ids are encoded by ChunkIdCodec as scope-qualified identifiers and resolved back to their parent record by IParentResolver / ChunkParentResolver — the parent-document recall pattern: retrieve the best chunk, return the whole record. Model-hash guard Embedding models define the geometry of their vectors. Mixing vectors produced by different models (or dimensions) in one index silently destroys retrieval quality. ProvostXMemory prevents this at three levels: Path isolation — index artifacts live under vectors/<model-hash>/ inside each scope, so a different model means a different artifact set. Options guard — VectorOptions carries the model hash and dimension; index files record them at build time. Runtime guard — IVectorIndexGuard implementations reject opens with a mismatched model hash or dimension, throwing VectorIndexGuardMismatchException instead of returning garbage. Consequence: swapping the embedding model is a data-migration decision, not a config flag. Re-embed and rebuild (RebuildAsync) under the new hash. See the FAQ. Namespaces The term namespace in this codebase means the scope-qualified partition that owns an artifact: a (scope, model-hash) pair for vectors, a scope for records/graph/lexical state. Query plans fan out across namespaces by targeting scope ids; fusion identifiers are scope-qualified so the same record id in two scopes never conflates (see Retrieval).

docs/consolidation.html.title: Consolidation | ProvostXMemory API
docs/consolidation.html.summary: Consolidation Consolidation is the maintenance pass that keeps a scope's memory healthy: deduplication, TTL expiry, and cluster-summary emission. It is triggered explicitly via IMemoryService.ConsolidateAsync(scope, options) — the library never mutates memory in the background on its own. What a pass does MemoryConsolidator (implements IMemoryConsolidator) runs over one scope: Deduplication — ThresholdDedupDetector (implements IDedupDetector) finds near-duplicates by embedding similarity at or above ConsolidationOptions.DedupSimilarityThreshold. Survivors are the oldest record; the survivor's tags are the union of the duplicate set's tags; newer duplicates are removed and their index artifacts are cleaned up. TTL expiry — when ConsolidationOptions.ExpireTtl is set, records whose ExpiresAt is in the past are deleted; expiry persists across restarts. Cluster summaries — when ConsolidationOptions.EmitClusterSummaries is set, ClusterSummarizer (implements IClusterSummarizer) produces a new summary record for each coherent cluster: the summary record is stored with category summary and appears in ordinary recall results; the cluster is also recorded in the scope's graph store (IMemoryGraphStore cluster write path), linking the member entities. The pass returns a report (via ConsolidationReportMeta) describing removals and emissions, and the facade refreshes or removes affected index artifacts so recall immediately reflects the consolidated state. Options reference Option Default Effect DedupSimilarityThreshold high (≈0.99999 used in journeys) Similarity at which two records are considered duplicates. ExpireTtl true Delete records past ExpiresAt during the pass. EmitClusterSummaries true Generate summary records + graph clusters. ConsolidationTuning exposes additional internal tuning knobs to the consolidator implementation. Policies and recommended cadence Threshold choice: set the dedup threshold as high as precision allows. At 0.99999+ only true restatements merge; lowering it aggressively risks collapsing distinct memories. When to run: after bulk ingestion, periodically for long-lived session scopes, and before eval runs that should measure consolidated-state quality. Ordering guarantees: consolidation is deterministic — the same store state and options produce the same survivors, unions, and summaries (pinned by tests, including non-regression of golden-query scores across a consolidation pass). Index consistency: you do not need to rebuild after consolidation; the facade refreshes index artifacts as part of the pass. A full RebuildAsync remains available for wholesale reindexing.

docs/evaluation.html.title: Evaluation | ProvostXMemory API
docs/evaluation.html.summary: Evaluation The ProvostXMemory.Eval package measures retrieval quality with standard ranking metrics, guards against regressions, and produces JSON reports. It is the same harness used by the library's own journey tests (golden-query recall gate at Recall@5 ≥ 0.9, achieved 1.0). Usage var factory = new DefaultEvalServiceFactory(vectorDim: 768); var runner = new EvalRunner(factory); var caseSet = new EvalCaseSet("release-notes", new[] { new EvalCase( CaseId: "q-01", Query: "kubernetes rollout", Scope: scope, RelevantIds: new[] { "note-1" }, RelevantKeys: Array.Empty<string>()) // optional key hints // ... }); EvalRunnerOptions options = new( TopK: 10, Thresholds: new EvalMetricThresholds(recallAtK: 0.9)); var report = await runner.EvaluateAsync(caseSet, options); The EvalServiceFactory abstraction builds a self-contained service (store, embedder, indexes) per evaluation; DefaultEvalServiceFactory composes the standard stack, and DeterministicEvalCorpus generates reproducible synthetic corpora (ClusterHashEmbedder provides deterministic embeddings with a fixed noise amplitude). disposeRootDirectory controls cleanup of the temporary root. Metrics Let R be the set of relevant record ids for a case, k the cut-off, and d(i) the rank position of the i-th relevant result in the returned ranking. Metric Formula Meaning Recall@k |R ∩ top-k| / |R| Fraction of relevant records found within the top k. Precision@k |R ∩ top-k| / k Fraction of the top k that is relevant. MRR (1/|R|) · Σ 1/d(i) Mean of reciprocal ranks of the first relevant hit (1.0 when the first result is relevant). NDCG@k DCG@k / IDCG@k, where DCG@k = Σi≤k gain(i)/log2(i+1) Discounted cumulative gain normalized by the ideal ranking; supports graded gains from per-hit traces. Metric math lives in EvalMetricMath (hand-verified against known answers, pinned by EvalMetricMathTests). Per-case results are EvalCaseMetrics; per-case hit traces (EvalCaseTrace, EvalCaseTraceHit) carry ids, scores, and gains. Reports EvalReportJson serializes a full report — aggregate metrics plus per-scope and per-stage breakdowns, threshold evaluations, and traces — in snake_case JSON. Round-trips are byte-identical (canonical rewrite), so reports diff cleanly in version control. Regression guarding EvalMetricThresholds declares per-metric floors: new EvalMetricThresholds(recallAtK: 0.90, mrr: 0.8); Violations are reported as MetricThresholdViolation entries (metric, actual, threshold) collected in MetricThresholdViolations. A non-empty violation list means the harness fails the run — wire it into CI as the recall-regression guard: fix the corpus and golden queries once, then any retrieval change that drops quality below the floors fails the build instead of shipping. Recommended practice: Keep golden queries per scope in version control (the EvalCaseSet is plain data). Pin thresholds slightly below observed baselines so noise does not flap. Diff serialized reports after intentional changes to see exactly which cases regressed.

docs/faq.html.title: FAQ | ProvostXMemory API
docs/faq.html.summary: FAQ How does scope isolation actually work? Isolation is structural. Every record, index, and graph artifact lives under its scope's resolved directory path (<root>/<scope-kind>/<scope-id>/…), every API operation is scope-bound, and query routing resolves indexes per scope through a scope-exact registry. A query in one scope has no code path that can read another scope's data. Cross-scope access happens only when you explicitly declare it via a QueryPlan fan-out. This is enforced at the storage, retrieval, and end-to-end levels by dedicated tests. Can I swap the embedding model? Yes, but it is a migration, not a toggle. Vectors are meaningless across models, so index artifacts are namespaced by model hash and guarded at open time (VectorIndexGuardMismatchException). To switch: configure a new model hash and dimension in VectorOptions and MemoryRootLayout, then re-embed and RebuildAsync(). Old artifacts under the previous hash remain on disk until you remove them. The library never downloads or selects models — the embedder is your injected IVectorEmbedder. Does it need a server? No. ProvostXMemory is an in-process library. Storage is transactional JSON/JSONL files under a root directory; the vector engine is pure C#. The only external integration points are the ones you inject (embedding model, optional grader/rewriter/reranker clients, optional external fetcher). What are the GPU requirements? None mandatory. The GPU layer (ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu, shipped in the single ProvostXMemory package) uses ILGPU kernels for Flat and IVF search, with lazy, exception-guarded accelerator discovery. On CPU-only machines — or with no compatible accelerator — the index transparently falls back to an injected CPU implementation with bit-identical results (identical accumulation order by construction). Configuring GPU unconditionally is therefore safe; the same conformance suite passes on CPU-only machines via the fallback. What is the persistence format? Human-readable files: JSONL for records (records.jsonl), JSON for manifests and FlatJson vector namespaces, JSONL for graph entities/relations/clusters. All writes go through AtomicFileWriter (temp file + atomic swap, optional fsync). Engine indexes persist their own artifact formats under vectors/<model-hash>/. Old-format record files are read forward-compatibly (Reps/Meta additions are backward-compatible). Is it thread-safe? Public facade operations are asynchronous and safe to call concurrently. Index mutation follows a build-or-rebuild model (HNSW indexes are immutable after build; mutations trigger batch rebuilds), which avoids the classic concurrent-mutation hazards. For heavy concurrent write workloads, serialize writes per scope as you would any transactional file store. Conformance tests exercise the documented behaviors; treat per-index instances as not thread-safe for concurrent mutation. How do I make recall results appear? Call BuildIndexesAsync(scope) after remembering records — index state is intentionally cold until built, and a fresh service over an existing root restores indexes via BuildIndexesAsync/RebuildAsync. Rankings after a rebuild are identical to before (determinism is tested). Which backend should I pick? Start with the zero-dependency FlatJson default. Move to the engine's FlatExact for SIMD-speed exact search, IVF at 10k–1M vectors when you accept a tunable recall trade-off, and HNSW at 10k–10M vectors for high-recall approximate search (measured recall@10 = 0.998). See Backends. Can I use my own reranker or grader? Yes — that is the design. Implement IReranker (or IRerankerClient for an external rerank service), IRetrievalGrader, and IQueryRewriter, and inject them. The library is LLM-agnostic: it orchestrates the corrective loop but never owns a model. How does consolidation decide what to delete? Deduplication keeps the oldest record of a near-duplicate cluster and unions the tags onto the survivor; TTL expiry deletes records past ExpiresAt; cluster summaries are additive (new summary-category records plus graph clusters). All decisions are deterministic for a given store state and options. See Consolidation. Does logging leak record content? No. IncludeContent defaults to false, and when disabled, record content never appears in any log output — enforced by content-leak tests. Log entries carry scope identity, category, timings, and correlation ids, not memory content. How do I verify logs have not been tampered with? Enable MemoryLogIntegrity.HashChain and periodically run LogChainVerifier.Verify(path). Each entry's hash covers its sequence number, timestamp, category, payload, and the previous entry's hash, so edits, deletions, and reordering are all detectable. See Logging. Can one record id exist in multiple scopes? Yes — ids are unique per scope, not globally, and query plans handle collisions via scope-qualified fusion identifiers so identical ids never conflate across scopes. What .NET version is required? .NET 8. There are no native library requirements beyond the .NET runtime; the GPU package adds the ILGPU runtime only if you reference it.

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | ProvostXMemory API
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started This guide walks through installing ProvostXMemory, wiring it into a host application, and selecting a vector index backend. Requirements .NET 8 (the library targets the .NET 8 SDK; any runtime compatible with .NET 8 works) No native dependencies, no external services, no database server. Storage is files on disk; the vector engine is pure C#. Install The public package id is ProvostXMemory (packaging is owner-gated; until published, reference the projects directly): dotnet add package ProvostXMemory Hosts reference only the root package. Optional backend packages are added when a non-default index kind is selected: Package Provides ProvostXMemory Facade, abstractions, storage, lexical, fusion, chunking, graph, consolidation, correction, reranking, retrieval, eval, logging, telemetry, FlatJson backend ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine Own vector engine: FlatExact (SIMD), IVF, HNSW ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Gpu ILGPU GPU kernels (Flat + IVF) with transparent CPU fallback First run using ProvostXMemory; using ProvostXMemory.Abstractions; using ProvostXMemory.Fusion; using ProvostXMemory.Storage; using ProvostXMemory.Telemetry; using ProvostXMemory.VectorIndex.Engine; var root = "/data/memory-root"; var layout = new MemoryRootLayout(root, "model-hash-v1"); IMemoryService memory = new MemoryServiceBuilder() .WithOptions(new MemoryServiceOptions( Storage: new StorageOptions(root), Vector: new VectorOptions("model-hash-v1", dim: 768, IndexKind.IndexKind.Hnsw), Graph: GraphOptions.Default, Fusion: new FusionOptions(), Consolidation: new ConsolidationOptions())) .WithStore(new JsonlMemoryStore(layout)) .WithEmbedder(embedder) // host-injected IVectorEmbedder .WithIndexFactory(new EngineVectorIndexFactory()) .WithFuser(new ReciprocalRankFuser()) .WithTelemetry(NoopMemoryTelemetry.Instance) .Build(); Everything the host injects is an interface: IVectorEmbedder (your embedding model), IVectorIndexFactory (the backend), optionally IRetrievalGrader, IQueryRewriter, IReranker, IEntityExtractor, IMemoryTelemetry, and IMemoryLogSink. The library never picks models or calls out to the network on its own. Write and read var scope = new MemoryScope(MemoryScopeKind.Session, "user-42"); await memory.RememberAsync(new MemoryRecord( "note-1", scope, "helm-rollout", "Kubernetes rollout notes…", Category: "ops", Tags: new[] { "infra", "deploy" })); await memory.BuildIndexesAsync(scope); RetrievalResult result = await memory.RecallAsync(new RetrievalQuery( "kubernetes rollout", scope, TopK: 5, Filters: new RetrievalFilters(Tags: new[] { "deploy" }))); foreach (var hit in result.Records) { Console.WriteLine($"{hit.Score:0.000} {hit.Record.Id}: {hit.Record.Key}"); } Key semantics to know on day one: BuildIndexesAsync(scope) must be called (or RebuildAsync() for all scopes) before recall returns results — index state is cold until built, and rebuilt deterministically after a restart. Every record, query, and index artifact is bound to a MemoryScope. A query in one scope can never return records from another. Dependency-injection wiring MemoryServiceBuilder is a fluent convenience wrapper; underneath it is plain constructor injection, so it composes naturally with any DI container: services.AddSingleton(sp => { var root = configuration["Memory:Root"]!; var layout = new MemoryRootLayout(root, configuration["Memory:ModelHash"]!); return new MemoryServiceBuilder() .WithOptions(new MemoryServiceOptions( Storage: new StorageOptions(root), Vector: new VectorOptions( configuration["Memory:ModelHash"]!, dim: 768, IndexKind.IndexKind.Hnsw), Graph: GraphOptions.Default, Fusion: new FusionOptions(), Consolidation: new ConsolidationOptions(), Logging: new MemoryLoggingOptions( Enabled: true, Level: MemoryLogLevel.Info, Sink: MemoryLogSinkKind.Injected, Integrity: MemoryLogIntegrity.HashChain))) .WithStore(new JsonlMemoryStore(layout)) .WithEmbedder(sp.GetRequiredService<IVectorEmbedder>()) .WithIndexFactory(new EngineVectorIndexFactory()) .WithFuser(new ReciprocalRankFuser()) .WithTelemetry(NoopMemoryTelemetry.Instance) .WithLogSink(sp.GetRequiredService<IMemoryLogSink>()) .Build(); }); services.AddSingleton<IMemoryService>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<MemoryServiceBuilder>().Build()); Register the embedder once; it is the single place where your embedding model enters the system. The model-hash in VectorOptions and MemoryRootLayout must match the model you inject — the library guards against dimension and model-hash mismatches when opening index artifacts (see Concepts). Backend selection Choose VectorOptions.IndexKind and the matching factory: Kind Factory Package Choose when Flat EngineVectorIndexFactory Engine Exact search up to ~10k vectors; SIMD-accelerated Ivf EngineVectorIndexFactory Engine 10k–1M vectors; small recall trade-off for much faster search Hnsw EngineVectorIndexFactory Engine 10k–10M vectors; approximate, high recall (measured 0.998 @10) Gpu GpuVectorIndexFactory Gpu Flat/IVF workloads with a compatible accelerator; falls back to CPU transparently default FlatJson core (no factory wiring needed beyond a scope-aware factory) core Zero-dependency persistence-first deployments; brute-force cosine per scope All backends implement the same IVectorIndex contract and pass an identical conformance suite, so switching is a configuration change, not a code change. See Backends for the full comparison.

docs/logging.html.title: Logging and Audit Hash-Chain | ProvostXMemory API
docs/logging.html.summary: Logging and Audit Hash-Chain ProvostXMemory ships a self-contained logging facility with an audit-grade integrity mode: append-only files, a SHA-256 hash chain for tamper evidence, rotation, retention, and strict content minimization. Disabled by default Logging is off by default with zero cost: no files are created, no allocations occur. Enable via MemoryServiceOptions.Logging: Logging: new MemoryLoggingOptions( Enabled: true, Level: MemoryLogLevel.Info, Sink: MemoryLogSinkKind.File, // File | Console | Injected Directory: Path.Combine(root, "logs"), FileNamePattern: "memory-{date}.log", Format: MemoryLogFormat.JsonLines, IncludeContent: false, // content NEVER logged by default Integrity: MemoryLogIntegrity.HashChain, RetentionDays: 30) Options reference Option Type / default Description Enabled bool, false Master switch. Disabled ⇒ no writes, no allocations. Level MemoryLogLevel, Info Minimum level emitted. Sink MemoryLogSinkKind, File File (rolling files), Console, or Injected (host-provided IMemoryLogSink via MemoryServiceBuilder.WithLogSink). Directory string Log directory (typically under the memory root). FileNamePattern string Rolling file name pattern. Format MemoryLogFormat, JsonLines Line format; MemoryLogJson provides the encoder. IncludeContent bool, false When false (default), record content never appears in any output — at most a short excerpt when explicitly enabled. Pinned by content-leak tests. Integrity MemoryLogIntegrity, HashChain Enables the SHA-256 audit hash chain. RetentionDays int? Retention window enforced by RetentionSweeper. Emitted categories Category Level Meaning Lifecycle info Service built; scope indexes opened. IndexBuild info Vector/lexical index builds per scope. Consolidation info Consolidation pass activity. ScopeRejection warn Store rejected an operation for a missing scope or record id. StoreError error Storage-layer failures. Each MemoryLogEntry carries a timestamp, monotonically increasing sequence number, level, category, optional MemoryLogScope (kind + id), correlation id, duration, and the chain fields. The audit hash chain When Integrity = MemoryLogIntegrity.HashChain, every entry is chained: entryHash(n) = SHA-256( sequence(n) ‖ timestamp(n) ‖ level ‖ category ‖ payload ‖ previousHash ) HashChainAppender computes and appends the chain; previousHash of entry n is entryHash(n-1), so any modification, deletion, or reordering of historical entries breaks every subsequent link. Verifying a log LogChainVerifier walks a log file (or stream) from the beginning and returns a LogChainVerificationResult: var verifier = new LogChainVerifier(); LogChainVerificationResult result = verifier.Verify(logFilePath); if (!result.IsValid) { // result.BrokenAtSequence: first sequence number where the chain broke // result.Detail: human-readable failure description } A valid result means the log is complete and unmodified from the first entry onward. This makes the log admissible as internal audit evidence: silent edits are detectable, and truncation is detectable as a chain break at the missing sequence. Retention and rotation RetentionSweeper deletes log files older than RetentionDays. Run it on your schedule (e.g. at service start) — retention is explicit, never implicit. Rotation follows FileNamePattern; rolling behavior is pinned by tests (FileRollingTests). Deleted log segments are not chains-compatible by design: if you must delete aged logs, delete whole files and treat each file as an independent chain (each file starts its own chain at sequence 0). Routing into host logging Use Sink: MemoryLogSinkKind.Injected plus MemoryServiceBuilder.WithLogSink(...) to forward MemoryLogEntry objects into your own logging pipeline. Note that hash-chain integrity applies to entries as emitted; if you need the chain, keep the file sink enabled as well.

docs/retrieval.html.title: Retrieval | ProvostXMemory API
docs/retrieval.html.summary: Retrieval How a query becomes an answer: the pipeline stages, when to use each retrieval route, and how filters apply. Pipeline overview RetrievalQuery (text, scope, topK, filters, plan?) | ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐ | MemoryService.RecallAsync routing | | plan → corrective → hybrid → rerank| └──────────────────┬──────────────────┘ | ┌───────────────┬───────────────┴────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ dense vector lexical (BM25) query plan fan-out search per search per scope across target scopes scope + key boost └───────┬───────┘ ▼ fusion (RRF, k=60 default; weighted dense/lexical) ▼ resolve vector/chunk ids → memory records (parent-document recall) ▼ filter enforcement (tags / category / date window) ▼ optional rerank (IReranker) ▼ corrective loop (when a grader is wired): grade → rewrite → retry ▼ RetrievalResult + diagnostics (per-stage scores, timings) Every stage is scope-exact. The scope index registry resolves the vector index, lexical index, and record provider for the query's scope; nothing from another scope enters the funnel. Hybrid retrieval (default route) HybridRetriever (implements IHybridRetriever) runs dense and lexical search in parallel for the query scope, then fuses: Dense — the query is embedded with the host's IVectorEmbedder and searched against the scope's vector index. Lexical — the tokenized query is scored against the scope's BM25 index (Bm25Scorer, saturated-TF IDF weighting plus a key-term boost). Fusion — ReciprocalRankFuser combines the ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (FusionOptions.RrfK, default 60) and configurable DenseWeight / LexicalWeight. Zero weights drop a stage entirely; a deterministic fallback ordering handles the all-zero edge case. Resolve — vector ids (including repr|… multi-representation ids and chunk ids) resolve back to records via the per-record id ledger and parent resolver. Rerank — if an IReranker is wired, candidates are re-scored after fusion. Use this route when you want the standard quality/speed balance with no extra infrastructure. Reranking Three built-in IReranker implementations: Reranker Behavior NoopReranker Pass-through; default when none is wired. ScoreBoostReranker Heuristic boosts for tag matches, key-term hits, and category matches; length-based penalties (ScoreBoostRerankerOptions). ClientBackedReranker Delegates to an IRerankerClient (your cross-encoder/LLM service) with a fallback IReranker; ClientBackedRerankerOptions.TrustClientCompletely controls whether client order is taken verbatim or fused with the fallback. The library stays LLM-agnostic: reranking intelligence is injected, never built in. Corrective loop CorrectiveRetriever (implements ICorrectiveRetriever) wraps the hybrid retriever with a self-checking loop: Retrieve candidates via the hybrid retriever. IRetrievalGrader grades each candidate Relevant | Irrelevant | Uncertain (host-injected — typically an LLM call). If evidence is weak (below CorrectionOptions.RelevanceFloor), IQueryRewriter (default KeywordQueryRewriter) rewrites the query and retries. If the result set is empty and UseFetcherOnEmpty is set, the injected IExternalFetcher is invoked — the extension hook for web augmentation. The library never fetches on its own. Use this route when recall quality matters more than latency, and you have a grading signal available. Graph retrieval The graph layer stores entities and relations extracted from memory records (via IEntityExtractor — HeuristicEntityExtractor ships in-box; hosts may inject an LLM-backed extractor) into a scope-pinned JsonlMemoryGraphStore. GraphRetriever (implements IGraphRetriever) maps a query to relevant entities, traverses Neighbors / ShortestPath, and returns records from the relevant subgraph together with GraphCluster summaries. Consolidation-emitted cluster summaries also surface in ordinary recall results as records with category summary and are linked as graph clusters. Use graph retrieval when questions are relational ("who is connected to X", "what cluster does this belong to") rather than purely similarity-based. Query plans A QueryPlan is a declarative, ordered list of QueryPlanStep entries, each with an Action, TargetScopes (scope ids to fan out to), and TopK. QueryPlanRunner executes the steps: Fan out retrieval across target scopes, with scope-qualified fusion ids so identical record ids in different scopes stay distinct. Merge step results through the fuser. One weak-evidence retry: if merged evidence is thin, the query is rewritten once (IQueryTextRewriter, default KeywordQueryTextRewriter) and re-executed. Use a plan when one logical question spans multiple scopes (e.g. a session scope plus its tenant parent) or when the agentic surface should express retrieval as data. MemoryService.RecallAsync routes to the plan runner automatically when RetrievalQuery.Plan is set. Filters RetrievalFilters supports tag sets, a single category, and a date window (From / To). Filters are enforced after candidate resolution (RetrievalFilterApplier), not merely hinted — filtering is pinned by dedicated enforcement tests. Filter on tags/category/date when the candidate set should be narrowed semantically and structurally. Diagnostics RetrievalResult.Diagnostics exposes per-stage scores and timings; IMemoryTelemetry receives the same signals for host-side observability. Stage names are stable constants (StageNames).

docs/scopes.html.title: Scopes and Multi-Tenancy | ProvostXMemory API
docs/scopes.html.summary: Scopes and Multi-Tenancy Scopes are the isolation unit of ProvostXMemory. This page covers scope kinds, the on-disk layout, hierarchy semantics, and patterns for multi-tenant hosts. Scope kinds MemoryScopeKind has five values; they are labels for intent, not behavior switches: Kind Typical use Platform Root scope of a host installation or product surface. Session One conversation / working session. Tenant One customer or organization in a multi-tenant host. Purpose A functional partition (e.g. curated long-term notes vs. scratch). Custom Host-defined partitioning. Path layout MemoryRootLayout resolves every scope to a unique directory subtree under the configured root: <root>/ manifest.json <scope-kind>/<scope-id>/ records.jsonl chunks/ vectors/<model-hash>/ index.json (FlatJson backend) index artifacts (Engine / GPU backends) graph/ entities.jsonl relations.jsonl clusters.jsonl Because isolation is implemented as path resolution, cross-scope access is structurally impossible: an operation bound to scope Session/user-42 never reads or writes outside Session/user-42/. There is no "global override", and none is needed — see the multi-tenancy patterns below for legitimate cross-scope aggregation. Hierarchy MemoryScope is (Kind, Id, ParentScope?): var tenant = new MemoryScope(MemoryScopeKind.Tenant, "acme"); var session = new MemoryScope(MemoryScopeKind.Session, "chat-1", tenant); session.Chain(); // [Tenant/acme, Session/chat-1] — outermost first tenant.Contains(session); // true session.Contains(tenant); // false Semantics pinned by tests: chains flatten outermost-first; Contains is reflexive and transitive over the chain; scopes are immutable (WithParent returns a copy). Persistence equality is kind + id — parent chains are host-side metadata used for Contains decisions and query-plan fan-out, and do not change where artifacts live. Multi-tenancy patterns Strict isolation (default). One scope per tenant; every RecallAsync and RememberAsync carries the tenant's scope. Nothing crosses. Use QueryPlan fan-out only when you deliberately want a merged view. Scoped aggregation via plans. To answer a question "over a tenant and the current session", issue a RetrievalQuery with a QueryPlan whose steps target both scope ids. The plan runner fuses results with scope-qualified ids — the same record id in two scopes stays distinct — and structural isolation is preserved because fan-out is an explicit, declared operation, not ambient access. Root + children. Model shared knowledge at the root (Platform) and per-context children beneath it (Tenant, Session). Children are separate scopes with their own artifacts; "inheritance" of knowledge is expressed as plan fan-out, not implicit reads. Enumeration. IMemoryService.Scopes() lists existing scopes under the root (via the store's IScopesAware hook, with a directory-layout fallback), enabling admin-style overviews without breaching per-scope read isolation. Testing your isolation story The library's test suite pins cross-scope invisibility at the storage, retrieval, and journey levels. For host-side confidence, assert in your own tests that a query scoped to tenant A never returns tenant B record ids — RecallAsync makes this a data assertion, no configuration required.

index.html.title: ProvostXMemory | ProvostXMemory API
index.html.summary: ProvostXMemory A strict-OOP, host-agnostic long-term memory library for .NET — scoped storage, hybrid (dense + lexical) retrieval with enforced filters, consolidation, graph, corrective recall, an eval harness, and audit-grade integrity-logged observability — over pluggable vector-index backends with an own C# engine and zero third-party vector dependencies. This is the site home of the generated offline documentation.
